News.title: Five children rescued from sea after getting trapped half a mile off shore as tide rose around them
News.content:
SEA RESCUE Five children rescued from sea after getting trapped half a mile off shore as tide rose around them

FIVE children have been rescued from the sea after getting trapped half a mile off the shore.

On Sunday at 4.45pm, the coastguard rushed to Shoebury East Beach in Essex to save a group children from disaster after the tide quickly began rising around them.



Southend-on-Sea RNLI volunteers launched its hovercraft H-004 Vera Ravine at 5pm and headed at top speed to the reported location at Shoeburyness.

They brought the cold children back to shore to be reunited with their worried parents.



The children were assessed after their rescue and thankfully escaped without any injuries.

Southend RNLI volunteer Commander Jonathan Charnock said: “Southend has a vast tidal flat area, at low tide whilst the water can be seen it can be over one mile from the shore.



“East Beach has the added danger of the MoD firing range to the east of the Boom.

“The children were found on their return to shore however they could have come into real danger quickly.

“With no way of calling for help, improper footwear and an unfamiliarity with the area today’s call could have had a very different outcome.

“If you do go onto the beaches of Southend, check out the local area, know where you can and can’t go.



“Tell someone your plan and a time, properly prepare and have a way of calling for help.”

News.title: Five people & ‘several’ pets found dead in ‘quintuple homicide’ after fire crews first called to Oregon home over blaze
News.content:
HORROR SCENE Five people & ‘several’ pets found dead in ‘quintuple homicide’ after fire crews first called to Oregon home over blaze

FIVE people and several pets have been found dead in a horror scene at a secluded rural property.

Firefighters made the grim discovery outside Forest Grove, Oregon, after initially being called to reports of a vehicle fire.



Crews arrived at the heavily-vegetated property on Northwest Otis Lane shortly after 5am on Saturday before spotting what appeared to be a body.

“We do have a deceased victim here. We are going to need law enforcement,” one firefighter was heard saying in dispatch audio obtained by ABC affiliate KATU.



Moments later, the scale of the unfolding horror became clearer.

“We need a police unit, or a sheriff’s office unit code 3 at the scene. Just in case, we have two victims here,” another transmission said.



A third firefighter added: “This is some suspicious circumstances certainly. So we’re going to take our hoses and get out of here, and let the sheriff’s office clear this.”

Washington County Sheriff’s Office deputies rushed to the property and ultimately discovered five people dead, along with multiple domesticated animals.

Cops are investigating the deaths as a quintuple homicide and have said all five victims were murdered.

The victims have not yet been publicly identified, and authorities have not revealed their ages or genders, how they died or where on the sprawling property their bodies were discovered.



Officials have also declined to say how many animals were killed or what kind they were.

Detectives later identified Benjamin Charles Parker, 36, as the suspect in the killings.

But the hunt for Parker came to an end Sunday when he was discovered dead inside his vehicle in Enumclaw, Washington.

“It is believed he died by suicide,” Sheriff Caprice Massey said.

“Detectives do not believe there is a danger to the public.”



Authorities have not revealed what relationship, if any, Parker allegedly had with the five victims.

Investigators have said they do not believe the killings were a random act of violence.

The scale and complexity of the crime scene sparked a huge response involving detectives, forensic experts, K9 teams and several other agencies.

Sheriff Massey said the horrific case was unlike anything she had encountered during more than two decades in the area.

“I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of, or witnessed, a scene quite this complex, involving this type of an investigation,” she said.



“And I’m just going to lead in and say that I recognize that this incident is deeply concerning to our community.

“Our investigators are working to determine what happened, and we have dedicated every available resource to this case.”

News.title: Massive fire rips through Gatwick Airport holiday parking site & industrial estate as man arrested over arson attack
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CAR INFERNO Massive fire rips through Gatwick Airport holiday parking site & industrial estate as man arrested over arson attack

A MASSIVE fire has ripped through a popular Gatwick Airport holiday parking site and industrial estate with cops arresting a man on suspicion of arson.

Police and firefighters scrambled to the scene of the blaze at Caldyne Business Park, West Sussex, just after 9pm on Saturday.

UK Power Network was forced to shut off power to more than 2,000 homes while crews tackled the incident at the industrial estate.

It is understood that the site is predominantly used for people parking their cars and heading to Gatwick Airport.





A number of cars are believed to have been damaged following the blaze.

The fire caused damage to high voltage equipment in the area.

A man has since been arrested on suspicion of arson and taken into custody.

Alongside eight fire engines, West Sussex Fire and Rescue sent two water carriers to the scene.



Nearby residents were advised over the weekend to keep windows and doors closed and members of the public were also asked to avoid the area.

However, no casualties have been reported.

Sussex Police said previously: “Power has been shut off to the immediate area, affecting a number of businesses and homes, and nearby roads remain closed as a precaution.

“A number of cars have also been damaged at a site used for holiday parking.



“Any affected consumers are advised to contact their operator directly.”

News.title: Swiss bar fire owner, 49, arrested over ‘violent attack on wife’ as pair face prison over deadly blaze that killed 41
News.content:
THE owner of the Swiss bar where 41 people died in a horror blaze on New Year’s has been arrested and held in custody for an alleged violent attack on his wife.

Jacques Moretti, 49, allegedly beat up his wife Jessica Moretti, 41, on August 11, putting her in hospital.



Both are facing trial for the huge fire that ripped through their bar Le Constellation, in the Swiss ski resort of Crans Montana, killing 41 revellers as they celebrated the start of 2026.

Moretti was arrested at their home in Valais, Switzerland, and “placed in pre-trial detention” an investigating source said.



He is now being held for several domestic violence charges and is set to appear in court later this year, Swiss and French media reported.

Moretti couple’s lawyers told reporters: “These events, being investigated in a separate case, pertain exclusively to their private life, and we will therefore make no comment.



“They should not be confused with the Constellation tragedy, but they nevertheless fall within a context that cannot be ignored: that of a particularly intense ordeal that the Morettis have been trying to face together since January 1.”

The trial will be separate to the one in which both Morettis face convictions for their alleged part in the bar fire, alongside 14 others, including local councillors who gave the couple licences.

Both were charged with “manslaughter by negligence, causing injury by negligence, and causing arson by negligence” charged after the horror blaze.

The fire killed 41 people and injured 115 others.



Jacques Moretti was the registered owner of the bar which his wife managed on the night of the fire.

Since her last hearing on June 5, Jessica Moretti has also been charged with forgery, relating to an invoice for sound-insulating foam panels in the bar.

Most of the casualties were teens, as the ski resort bar was popular with young people.



Terrified New Year’s Eve revellers were left “screaming and running” for their lives as they were trapped inside the bar as an inferno tore through the basement club.

Eyewitness Bastien Frema, 20, said: “People were screaming. I saw people with burnt clothing shredded, hanging off them.

“People were yelling, trying to get help. We couldn’t do anything.”

Another said: “It was mayhem. People were so badly burned. No one knew what was happening.”

On fire safety, Jacques Moretti admitted: “There was no training, but employees were told what steps to take in case of fire when they were shown around the premises.



“Evacuate the customers, raise the alarm, and call the fire department. And of course, if they had time, use the fire extinguishers to put out the fire.”

When told one worker had no idea where extinguishers were kept, he replied: “The staff has several shifts, and maybe I forgot to give this information… Maybe I forgot.”

The couple also blamed an unnamed staff member for allegedly locking a basement emergency exit.

Moretti reportedly told investigators that he found a pile of bodies on the floor when he unlocked the door after the deadly blaze.

He was briefly held in a cell in connection with the fire on January 9, but released on bail.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 2008, he was sentenced to a year in prison, with eight suspended, for “aggravated pimping”.

The criminal investigations into the fire, and the alleged domestic abuse, continue.

News.title: Acrobat who suffered devastating injuries including broken bones after horror 15ft plunge is now SUING circus for £12m
News.content:
AN ACROBAT is suing Cirque du Soleil for a whopping £12million after plunging 15 feet during a performance without a safety net underneath.

Russian Mariia Konfektova, who holds the Guinness World Record for most seated aerial hoop rotations in 30 seconds, sustained multiple injuries in the “life-changing” fall during the Kooza show in Portland, Oregon.



Footage shows her suspended in the air, spinning on a ring, when she lost her grip and plummeted face-first on the hard stage floor.

A personal injury lawsuit has finally detailed the full extent of her injuries – 11 broken bones, fractures to her lower back, wrist, skull and at least seven bones in her face, as well as a concussion and double vision.



Konfektova had to undergo multiple surgeries, The Oregonian reported.

She said she has been left with permanent injuries, according to the lawsuit.

As a result, the artist is seeking the whopping sum from the largest contemporary circus producer in the world.

According to the lawsuit, Cirque du Soleil did not provide adequate safety equipment, including mats, nets or other equipment to mitigate harm from a fall.

It also alleged that Cirque du Soleil ignored concerns the performer raised about the rigging for the hoop she fell from, and that the circus fired her when she returned to work and continued raising safety concerns after the accident.

A GoFundMe set up by the artist detailed how she continues to live with “persistent double vision and other long-term complications”.



“Although I survived and worked hard to recover, I continue to live with persistent double vision and other long-term complications,” Konfektova said.

“Recent medical evaluations confirmed ongoing problems affecting my vision, jaw, facial symmetry, breathing, and daily life…”

She added: “Unfortunately, ongoing medical, insurance, legal, and immigration complications have made my situation increasingly difficult.



“My access to treatment remains uncertain, and I cannot fully return to my profession while my future surgeries are still ahead of me.”

Konfektova is among 16 performers who have suffered notable injuries during their career with Cirque du Soleil over the past 20 years.

The Oregonian reported that three were so catastrophic that the victims died – in Montreal in 2009, Las Vegas in 2013 and Tampa in 2018.

Almost all of the accidents involved falls ranging from 10 feet to 94 feet.

Shortly after the frightening fall, Cirque du Soleil said Konfektova was “recovering and being cared for by our medical and coaching team”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A statement explained she had fallen on her head and was hospitalised, but left the full extent of her injuries unclear.

The Sun has reached out to Cirque du Soleil for a comment.

News.title: Five arrested as cops shut down illegal rave in quaint rural village
News.content:
RAVING MAD Five arrested as cops shut down illegal rave in quaint rural village

FIVE people have been arrested after police shut down an illegal rave in a sleepy rural village.

The quiet town was plunged into chaos in the early hours of Sunday as furious locals were kept awake due to the raucous unlicensed event.



Local police received reports of a disturbance shortly after 1am on Sunday near Thursford Road in Little Snoring.

But nearby residents were doing anything but snoring as the noisy rave went on – with many complaining of the loud music on social media.



Cops rushed to the scene near Fakenham, seizing sound equipment, vehicles and generators.

Officers also closed the entrance to the venue in order to prevent further people from attending.

The event was monitored closely by authorities all throughout the night and into the early hours of Sunday morning.

Ravers were then ordered to leave and disperse.

By late morning, many had begun to leave the site.

The five suspects were cuffed in connection with the event on suspicion of offences including drug driving, drink driving, possession of a class A with intent to supply and carrying on a licensable activity without a licence.



An investigation has been launched to identify who organised the event.

Superintendent Craig Miller said: “We are committed to doing everything we can to prevent, disrupt and stop these events from taking place, while reducing their impact on local communities.

“I would like to thank the landowner and members of the local community for their patience and understanding while we worked to shut down the event as quickly and safely as possible.

“Unauthorised music events such as this can cause significant disruption and often result in damage to the natural environment. As they are not required to meet recognised safety standards, they can also place attendees at risk.

“Our work does not end with the closure of the event, and investigations into those responsible and the circumstances surrounding it will continue.”



Patrick Galbraith, a Great Snoring local, told Eastern Daily Press he went to the site of the rave on Sunday morning.

He said an officer told him they needed riot shields to break up the event.

The resident said: “The people at the rave were very friendly.

“A young raver apologised for snorting a white substance off his phone in front of me.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “I later bumped into the police who said they could not ‘go down there’ without riot shields.



“This surprised me as there were not that many ravers.”

News.title: Andy Burnham to handover blueprints for Storm Shadow missiles to Ukraine as he arrives in Kyiv for first visit as PM
News.content:
ANDY Burnham will hand over blueprints for Storm Shadow missiles to Ukraine as he arrives in Kyiv for his first visit as Prime Minister.

He has vowed Britain will stand with Ukraine “for as long as it takes” as he visits the capital to mark its Independence Day alongside President Zelensky.



The PM arrived this morning and has agreed to provide Ukraine with blueprints to produce long-range missiles.

Mr Burnham will allow European defence firm MBDA to declassify information on UK components for the Scalp missile – the French-produced version of the UK’s Storm Shadow.



The “deep precision strike” missiles use shared French and British technology, and Ukraine and France are looking to set up local assembly lines to produce them in Ukraine.

Mr Burnham will also chair his first meeting of the UK and France-led Coalition of the Willing.



The PM said: “The friendship between our two countries will long outlast Russia’s illegal war.

“In both the fight and in the rebuilding to come, we will stand with Ukraine.



“And deliver opportunities for people across both our countries.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve.

“We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

During his visit, Burnham will also take part in Independence Day events and accept an award on behalf of the British people recognising the UK’s support.



Mr Burnham is set to assure Ukrainians of the UK’s backing and reiterate that Russia’s threats only strengthen British resolve.

He added: “On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.

“I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver.

“After all, Ukraine’s security is our security.”

It comes after Moscow warned Britain would face “consequences” over the reported use of UK-made drones in Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russia.



Last week, Russia said the deeper the country’s involvement became, “the higher the price it will pay”.

News.title: Man, 52, dies after horror double stabbing at seaside town – as cops arrest suspect, 21, and launch murder probe
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KNIFE HORROR Man, 52, dies after horror double stabbing at seaside town – as cops arrest suspect, 21, and launch murder probe

COPS have launched a murder probe after a man died in a horror seafront stabbing.

The brutal attack is said to have happened in the early hours – at around 4.45am – in the harbour area of Ramsgate, Kent.



Police were called after reports of a man carrying a knife.

Officers and paramedics rushed to the scene and found two men suffering injuries consistent with being stabbed.



A 52-year-old man was found injured in Harbour Street, while a 48-year-old was discovered in nearby Harbour Parade.

Both were rushed to a local hospital with serious injuries.



But the 52-year-old was later pronounced dead.

His next of kin have been informed.

The second victim has since been discharged from hospital.

A 21-year-old British man was arrested shortly afterwards and remains in custody as detectives probe the horror.



Cops are not looking for anyone else in connection with the attack.

Large parts of the harbour remain cordoned off, including Harbour Street and sections of the seafront near the Royal Victoria Pavilion Wetherspoon pub.

Forensics officers have been scouring the scene, with investigators seen working inside the cordon on Harbour Street.

A taxi believed to be linked to the incident is also being examined after it crashed onto concrete bollards on the pavement near the seafront, Kent Online reports.

A forensic officer was seen photographing the cab as the investigation continued this morning.



Pictures from the scene show the taxi partially mounted on the bollards, with police tape surrounding the area.

Several businesses in Harbour Street, including the Silver Compass Sports Bar, have been unable to open.

Kent Police said inquiries into the circumstances of the stabbing are continuing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Extra patrols will also be carried out across Ramsgate today.

Anybody with information is asked to contact Kent Police, quoting reference 46/139262/26.

News.title: Murder investigations launched as five bodies found by police on rural Oregon property
News.content:
Murder investigations launched as five bodies found by police on rural Oregon property

WARNING DISTRESSING CONTENT: The gruesome discovery was made in the US state of Oregon, after emergency services were called to a vehicle fire at the weekend

View 2 Images File photo of American police (Image: Getty Images)

Police have launched multiple murder investigations after t he bodies of five people were found on a rural property on Sunday.

‌



The gruesome discovery was made at a home outside Portland, Oregon. Police were initially called early on Saturday (August 22) to reports of a vehicle fire at a property in Forest Grove, about 30 miles west of downtown Portland.

‌



Responders then found the remains of five people and “several domestic animals". Detectives do not believe it was a random act of violence.

‌



Few details have emerged in the case, but no arrests have been made and no one is in custody. Authorities also did not disclose the ages or genders of the people found, how they died, or what possible connections they might have with one another.

The type of animals found dead also was not specified. At a news conference Sunday afternoon (August 23), Detective Shannon Wilde with the sheriff’s office said they were still working to determine who the victims were.

‌



“Any time you have one person deceased, let alone five, that’s a logistical challenge,” Wilde said, noting the complexity of the investigation and the large crime scene.

View 2 Images The discovery was made 30 miles west of downtown Portland, Oregon's largest city (Image: Getty Images)

When asked by reporters about the amount of time that passed between authorities first discovering the dead bodies and releasing information the following afternoon, Wilde said authorities were trying to identify the victims and notify their next of kin before holding a news conference while also working on a “very active investigation with a lot of moving pieces.” Authorities wanted to ensure they released accurate information in a responsible way, she said.

Article continues below

Sheriff Caprice Massey urged anyone who is familiar with the property or the people who live there to share any information they may have.

“I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex involving this type of an investigation,” she said.

News.title: 'We got breast cancer in our 20s like thousands more, screening needs to change'
News.content:
'We got breast cancer in our 20s like thousands more, screening needs to change'

EXCLUSIVE: As a study finds that 95 percent of high-risk women under 50 are being missed when it comes to breast cancer screening rules, The Mirror speaks to three patients who were all diagnosed with the disease before becoming eligible for mammograms

View 7 Images Both Lily and Alex were diagnosed with breast cancer in their twenties

Breast cancer is the fourth most common cause of cancer death in the UK, but according to an alarming new report, NHS screening criteria means up to 95 percent of higher-risk women under 50 are being missed.

‌



Women over 50 are offered a routine mammogram scan to check their breasts, but since the early 1990s, the rate of breast cancer in women under 50 has soared by 20 percent, making it the leading cause of cancer-related death among women aged 25 to 49 in the UK.

‌



According to National Institute of Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines, women under 50 can only be referred for screening if they have a strong family history or diagnosed genetic mutations, such as BRCA1. But a study by Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research - based on a new risk assessment tool - identified eight times as many women under 50 who developed the disease. Seventy percent of women under 50 who develop breast cancer have no known family history.

‌



Emotional Lucy Davis hopes for miracle treatment as she speaks to other women with cancer READ MORE :

7 View 7 Images Lily was shocked to find out she had cancer after being assured there was nothing to worry about (Image: Daily Mirror) 7 View 7 Images Now out of her recovery, Lily shares her journey online and helping other women

Lily Ward, 27, had an itch on her breast before she noticed a lump the size of a blueberry. Her doctor initially thought it was a fibroadenoma - a noncancerous (benign) solid breast lump of tissue - and assured her it was nothing to worry about. She was told to come back if it got bigger. Three months later she returned and was cleared after an ultrasound. the same happened on her third visit three months later.

Asked about family history, she told doctors there was nothing from her mum's side but a strong history of cancer on her dad's side. Again, she says she felt ignored.

‌



By her fourth visit the lump was significantly bigger and her nipple had changed. Lily saw a different consultant and was told it needed to be removed - but that there was still nothing to worry about.

Just over a year later, Lily underwent surgery and was horrified to learn that it was cancer and another lump had been found underneath. Not only that, but it had spread to her lymph nodes.

"I do wonder if they would have removed it quicker if there was a history of breast cancer on my mum's side, because thats all they seemed to worry about was my mum's side," Lily, a hairdresser from Suffolk told Daily Mirror.

‌



CT scans, MRI's, and blood tests followed, which revealed she has the BRCA2 gene mutation. "So many thoughts then went through my mind, why me? What have I done so wrong in life to get this at such a young age? Will I be beat this? How do I tell my family and friends this awful news?

"I then had the double masectomy in the November, I had six months of chemotherapy and the immunotherapy and then the surgey for the double masectomy and then had three weeks of radiotherapy after surgery and is now waiting for resconstruction surgery.

She then decided to share her cancer journey publicly, so she could help others who may be the same age. "I felt so alone going through this at such a young age that I thought if I could help anyone similar age to me not to feel alone via my page then that would be amazing, so I changed my page to public.

‌



"There definitely needs to be more done for testing younger people and acknowledging that they can get breast cancer young."

A study published in the British Journal of Cancer found that one in seven women develop breast cancer in their life, but only 5-10 percent of cases are linked to inherited genes. The other 90 to 95 percent of cases are triggered by a combination of non-inherited factors such as breast density, early menstruation, exercise, weight and other lifestyle factors.

Laura Marfell-William's turned 50 on May 18, and was just on the cusp of being eligible for screening when she found a lump on her breast on May 29. With no symptoms, Laura, a travel PR, from Norfolk, said she could have easily missed it. "I do check probably once a month normally in the shower. But it just so happened that I was worn out from my birthday week I was just lying on the bed watching a film and I just scratched my side and thought 'oh what's that?' so I called my doctors and they got back to me within ten minutes."

‌



View 7 Images Laura felt her lump on her breast just weeks after 50th birthday

Laura was then diagnosed with breast cancer after a mammogram, ultrasound and biopsy and three further lumps were found on her other breasts.

"Based on the conversations that I've had with people as a result of my diagnosis, the amount of other people my age, or a couple of years either side that I didn't know had breast cancer, and it seems that either they picked up purely by chance or because they felt it. I definitely think they need to lower the age for the screenings."

‌



The study by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looked at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women and used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score, according to the BBC.

It found that if all women under 50 were assessed using the tool, around a quarter would be classed as 'above average' and referred for more tests. Currently under the NICE guidelines, only 1 in 70 women under 50 qualify for specialist assessment or preventative care.

Lily said since sharing her cancer journey, she's found so many other girls a similar age to herself also being diagnosed. "I really think something needs to be done about lowering the age. I think a lot of us have almost had to fight to get diagnosed and there needs to be more done with education that younger people can get breast cancer."

‌



Similarly, Alex Reddington was diagnosed with breast cancer in April 2025 aged just 26, and is now coming to the end of her treatment over a year later.

When in the shower, Alex, who works in commercial services for ITV and lives in London, checked and found a lump in her left breast. As a swimmer, Alex put it down to an injury from intense swimming sessions a few days before. Believing it to be a bump or muscle, she didn't think much of it.

7 View 7 Images Alex Reddington was just 26 when she got diagnosed with breast cancer 7 View 7 Images She has finished her chemotherapy and radiation and wants to help young women be more aware of the symptoms

‌



Alex revealed that it was seeing Lorraine Kelly's Breast Cancer awareness promotion stickers plastered around her office that prompted her to check her breasts. After three weeks, the lump was still there and she booked in to see her GP. "I'd never thought to check my breasts before and I've never had any history of breast cancer in my family and no genetic dispositions, I was perfectly healthy up until I was diagnosed with cancer. I never considered breast cancer would have been something to consider but when I saw it [the lump] I thought I should go and check it," she said.

"I wasn't entirely dismissed, but I was given the impression it wasn't anything to worry about," she said. "She had said given my age and family history it probably wasn't something serious. She said it may have been a cyst and gave me the option to see a specialist who could do a little more investigating.

"I very easily could have said no, but I thought why not and three weeks later, while waiting for the biopsy they told me it was most likely to be breast cancer."

‌



Alex was left in shock when she was officially diagnosed after mammograms and a biopsy. "It was only when I spoke to my mum when the concern hit me. There were a lot of emotions and I didn't really know how to feel."

View 7 Images Alex pictured ringing the bell, signalling the end of her treatment

Alex believes the age for testing should be lowered, calling 50 "too old" to start getting checked. "I've met so many people who have been diagnosed under 50. I think there needs to be more awareness of how to check as well."

‌



Since documenting her journey, Alex has shared lots of tips and information to younger women on how to check their breasts and what signs to look out for. "It's free and you can do it whenever. Women just need to be taught from a young age how to feel comfortable with what their breasts feel like and what to look like. The more familiar you are, the easier you are to recognise when something is wrong.

"If you smoke you wouldn't be surprised if you had lung cancer, but I didn't have anything and never considered having cancer in my twenties."

After 15 rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, she is on the road to recovery: "It's definitely lingering, but it's momentum in the right direction."

‌



Dr Sowmiya Moorthie, senior strategic evidence manager at Cancer Research UK, told the Daily Mirror that more needs to be done to give younger women the tools to manage their personal risk, but that change needs to be managed respinsibly.

"Exploring different ways to identify women with a higher risk of breast cancer could help people receive more personalised care. The current UK approach, which relies on women under 50 self-presenting, misses many women with a higher risk of breast cancer who could benefit from targeted support and guidance on how to manage their risk.

"Further research is needed, however, to understand the impact of adopting a different approach, including on staffing and equipment. Any changes must be accessible and equitable, taking into consideration the anxiety that extra referrals might cause for women. Everyone can take steps to reduce their cancer risk, such as maintaining a healthy weight and cutting back on alcohol. Anyone who notices a change that is unusual for them should speak to their GP, as early diagnosis can improve outcomes."

Article continues below

A NICE spokesperson said that despite the findings, there are no plans to update screening guidelines.

"NICE welcomes the findings of this study and recognises the potential of multifactorial risk models in improving the identification of women at increased risk of breast cancer in the future," they said.

"However, the current evidence does not warrant a change to our existing familial breast cancer guideline at this time. NICE remains committed to reviewing new evidence and will consider further updates as more data on feasibility and clinical outcomes become available."

News.title: Mum's anger after children find pills in holiday park caravan
News.content:
Mum's anger after children find pills in holiday park caravan

Imogen says she had already complained that the accommodation had not been properly cleaned

View 4 Images The pills found in the cupboard

A mum claims she fled a ‘nightmare' holiday park after her children found loose prescription tablets in the bedroom of her caravan. Imogen’s children, aged six and seven, allegedly found the medication inside a low bedside cupboard at Littlesea Holiday Park, near Weymouth, Dorset.

‌



The 30-year-old said the youngsters opened the cupboard themselves before screaming for her. Pictures taken inside the caravan appear to show several loose white tablets, including a large capsule-shaped pill bearing the imprint “XR 1000”.

‌



Imogen immediately removed the tablets, photographed them and handed them to staff at the park reception. She said: “Finding those tablets made my blood run entirely cold. If either of my children had mistaken those white pills for sweets and swallowed them, it could have caused a catastrophic medical emergency.

‌



View 4 Images Imogen says parts of the accommodation were dirty

“As a mother, knowing how close my babies came to being poisoned is a living nightmare.”

‌



The “XR 1000” marking is used on some 1,000mg extended-release metformin products. UK medicines guidance says a large metformin overdose can cause lactic acidosis, a medical emergency requiring hospital treatment.

Imogen said she had already complained through the Haven app about dead insects, cobwebs, a dirty fridge, debris on the floor and marks across the cupboards. A cleaner was subsequently sent back to the accommodation. Imogen also reported a broken kitchen kickboard, bin lid, curtain rail and gate. She said one maintenance worker attended on the Friday but was unable to repair the gate, before another employee returned and fixed it the following day.

The mum said her son also developed a rash on his neck during the holiday. She said: “Beyond the drugs, the accommodation was neglected and thoroughly filthy upon arrival.

‌



View 4 Images A rash that developed on the back of Imogen's son's head

“We had to waste our precious holiday time waiting around because they had to send a cleaner back to the caravan. The hygiene standards were so appalling that my son broke out in a physical skin rash on his neck.”

‌



Imogen said she initially received an apology when she handed the tablets to reception. She claims she heard nothing further about the medication until speaking to a manager the next day.

She claims that when she asked for the discovery to be formally recorded as a health and safety incident, the manager replied: “I won’t be doing that as I don’t need to.”

Imogen said she felt “cornered” into accepting an offer of a 50 per cent refund during the discussion. She said she later wrote to Haven rejecting the suggestion that the complaint had been resolved.

‌



The mum left the park at approximately 4.15pm on Sunday, 16 August, earlier than planned.

View 4 Images A broken curtain rail

‌



She said: “I fled the park to protect my family’s health. I have completely lost all faith in Haven Holidays.”

Mateusz Dolata, general manager of Littlesea, subsequently apologised to Imogen in an email He wrote: “A prescription tablet should never have been left in a holiday home and I am truly sorry for this.”

Mr Dolata said the tablets were disposed of appropriately and the incident was later logged on the company’s system so it could be investigated. He said Imogen accepted a 50 per cent refund worth £320 and remained at the park until Sunday evening.

Article continues below

Mr Dolata said Friday had been exceptionally hot and cleaning teams had been working in “very challenging conditions”. He added that this may explain the missed check but was “not an excuse”.

He said the matter had been followed up with the relevant employee and would be used to reinforce the importance of checking every part of the company’s holiday homes. Mr Dolata added: “I am genuinely sorry for the distress and worry caused and I completely appreciate why finding medication in your accommodation would have been particularly upsetting as a parent.”

Haven has been approached for further comment.

News.title: 'I thought I had food poisoning from Egypt holiday but I was seriously ill'
News.content:
'I thought I had food poisoning from Egypt holiday but I was seriously ill'

The 30-year-old put her symptoms down to a holiday bug, but then they kept getting worse

View 4 Images Rafiya Sherin came hoemn from holiday with 'dizziness'

A woman who thought her symptoms were a holiday food poisoning bug picked up in Egypt was told she actually had a life-threatening disorder. Rafiya Sherin had been away in Egypt with friends when she returned home with an unshakeable dizziness.

‌



The 30-year-old believed it could be linked to a bout of food poisoning she had while away. But, as her symptoms began to worsen, including sickness, muscle pain, fatigue and diarrhoea, she decided to get help.

‌



At hospital, she was told her bone marrow had failed; meaning it wasn’t producing any new blood cells. “It’s a scary prospect, as I’m a very social person,” said the marketing manager, from Preston.

‌



View 4 Images Rafiya needed treatment the same day

“I love my work and being out and interacting with other people is an important part of who I am. The idea that I’m too ill to work or be around my friends and family has been hard to deal with.”

‌



Rafiya’s symptoms began while on holiday in Sharm El Sheikh, Egypt, in June 2026. After the diagnosis, she had an emergency blood transfusion the same day. Multiple tests followed and 10 days later it was confirmed she had severe aplastic anaemia.

It’s a life-threatening disorder which affects around 100 people each year, according to blood cancer charity DKMS UK. Without treatment, it’s usually fatal and those affected are given a few months, up to a year.

View 4 Images Rafiya Sherin was told her bone marrow had failed

‌



Now, to give her a second chance at life, she’s working with the charity in a bid to find a stem cell donor. As Rafiya is from an ethnic minority background, a match is few and far between.

She said: “Finding out about the register was a relief for me. I’m glad that it exists and that people can join to find out if they can help me or someone else in my position. But I’m also glad that I can use my story to encourage people to sign up.

‌



“It’s a scary diagnosis, but knowing that there is an easy, practical way that people can help, has given me a sense of purpose in my treatment. I hope that, in the future, when someone from an ethnic minority receives a diagnosis like mine, they’ll feel a little less frightened knowing they have a better chance of finding a match because more people joined the register.”

Anyone aged 16-55 – and in general good health – can sign up. Currently, just seven percent of the eligible population in the UK are registered.

View 4 Images Rafiya is raising awareness

‌



And, only 16% of the register is from an ethnic minority background; leaving Rafiya, and others of non-white heritages, with a less chance of finding their life-saving match. Rafiya is now reliant on regular blood transfusions and goes for monitoring multiple times a week.

She said: “It would mean the world to me and my family to see lots of people register. For someone like me, and for so many others waiting for a stem cell donor, every new person who joins the register could be someone’s second chance at life.

Article continues below

“I honestly don’t think there’s an easier way to save someone’s life than this. It costs nothing financially, and, for most people, requires so little. Even if someone isn’t a match for me, they could go on to save another person and another family from going through what we’re facing.

“Seeing our community come together with such kindness and hope would mean more than words can say.”

News.title: Missing woman, 24, is found by police chained to bed in ex-boyfriend's home
News.content:
Missing woman, 24, is found by police chained to bed in ex-boyfriend's home

Emiliane Tamara Nunes Carvalho, 24, was found by police after reportedly being held hostage by her ex boyfriend for five days and chained by her neck

View 2 Images Ailton Rodrigues de Souza was arrested after the woman was found (Image: Police)

A woman was found by police chained by her neck in awful conditions at her ex-boyfriend's house after allegedly being abducted.

‌



Emiliane Tamara Nunes Carvalho, 24, was found at a property in Brazil after reportedly being held hostage for five days by her ex partner.

‌



Carvalho was reported missing on August 17 after her family said she failed to return from a doctor’s appointment.

‌



Police found the woman tied up with ropes and handcuffs at a property in Águas Lindas de Goiás.

The force said she struggled to breathe when she was found after she was allegedly kidnapped by her ex-boyfriend Ailton Rodrigues de Souza.

View 2 Images Police forced their way into the home after reports the woman was missing (Image: Police )

‌



The suspect reportedly staged his own disappearance to divert attention, according to police. The force claim that he kidnapped Emiliane and held her captive after she broke up with him.

Videos shared by the force show the shocking discovery of the woman after they forcefully cut their way into the home.

Police are then shown to make their way to a room at the back of the property and kick down the door.

‌



Inside, the woman can be seen shaking as she is tied to a mattress with several ropes and chains - in the footage she also appears to have a mask and a gag attached to her face.

Emiliane was taken to hospital and posted on social media on Saturday that she was released but is still recovering from her injuries.

She claimed that she is still under medication and that her wounds had affected her ability to see. She also alleged she had been assaulted while inside the property and her ex-partner used burning cloths to torch her skin.

‌



Souza's own family reported him as missing too, which made the police's suspicions grow.

He was arrested on the day Emiliane was found.

After raiding the run-down home where Emiliane was found, officers seized a 9mm pistol, sedatives, and items used to restrain the alleged victim.

Article continues below

The investigation continues.

News.title: Donald Trump facing staff exodus as they see 'writing on the wall' for four key reasons
News.content:
Donald Trump facing staff exodus as they see 'writing on the wall' for four key reasons

The midterms are looming and some in the White House are jumping ship, leaving the President with a growing number of departures - so what does this mean for Trump?

View 4 Images US President Donald Trump (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump is facing a growing mass departure of White House staff, with a string of senior aides preparing to walk as the US President looks down the barrel of what may be a rather turbulent second half of his presidential term.

‌



Several key figures have announced their departures in recent weeks, raising questions over the stability of Trump's inner circle ahead of the midterm elections.

‌



James Braid, a senior White House liaison to Congress, is due to leave his post on September 30, according to Politico. Last week, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced her departure, while Trump has confirmed that pardon attorney Ed Martin is leaving for the private sector. Their exits follow the announcement that White House counsel Dave Warrington is also stepping down.

‌



View 4 Images White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

While staff departures are not unusual in Washington with a midterm election on the horizon, Trump likes to keep his inner circle small. His reliance on a crack team of key staffers and fiercely loyal aides could mean he feels the losses even more than most other presidents in his shoes – and it may pose a greater headache for the 47th US President.

One former Trump administration official told Politico that some people were already "seeing the writing on the wall" and questioning whether Republicans would retain control of Congress.

‌



The official said: "I think people are seeing the writing on the wall and thinking Republicans probably aren't going to have the House, might not have the Senate either, and things are going to be stalled."

They added that officials were increasingly considering their prospects once they leave government.

"People are thinking, 'what are my post-administration business prospects? Is it worth taking these hits every single day, being part of these battles, and how does that hurt my prospects when I go to the private sector?'"

‌



According to Politico, there are four key reasons being cited for the departures. Staff are thinking about their next jobs and their "marketability".

"If you want a decent job downtown, you need to bounce now, because there are still relationships to trade on in the majority," the person said.

‌



View 4 Images U.S. President Donald Trump (Image: Getty Images)

The concern is that if Republicans lose one or both chambers of Congress, the influence of current White House officials could drop off sharply. That loss of influence would make finding their next gig even tougher for White House staffers who may depart in the second half of Trump's term – essentially, their government experience and political contacts will be less of a bargaining chip for any jobs in the private sector.

The looming midterms are another major factor.

‌



There is growing speculation within Trump's orbit that Republicans could lose control of the House and potentially the Senate.

A Democratic-controlled Congress could essentially see a Trump government hamstrung by investigations, subpoenas and oversight. Legislation would also become tougher for the White House to push through.

For the senior roles that already need to be filled in the White House, some will require around-the-clock commitment – especially for anyone wishing to step into Leavitt's shoes.

‌



She has already said the relentless workload was a large part of her decision to relinquish her role after returning to work following the birth of her second child.

Leavitt added she had realised she could not be "the best mom" her two young children deserved while devoting the "constant time, energy, and attention" required by the press secretary role.

Leavitt's comments seem to hint that being a close confidant to the US President comes at a gruelling personal toll of the 24/7 variety.

‌



View 4 Images White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt speaks during a press briefing on August 12 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Others seem to be wondering if remaining at the White House is worth it – both personally and professionally.

White House staffers under Trump face a relentless stream of political battles, scrutiny, and controversy, with the US President's senior aides and inner circle expected to defend him and his agenda on a daily basis.

‌



One person close to the administration told Politico that it will come down to whether officials want to keep taking hits on Trump's behalf if doing so could ultimately damage their future career prospects.

Despite the latest round of exits, Trump's second term has been notable for aides and White House staffers staying largely put.

White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers defended the administration's record, saying: "President Trump has built the greatest political movement in history, staffing his administration with talented, dedicated patriots who work tirelessly to execute his agenda." She added: "This movement is bigger than any one staff member, and the President's mission to make America greater than ever before will continue unabated."

Article continues below

Political analyst Chris Whipple described the coming period as "choppy" and "treacherous waters" for the US President, with Trump likely to struggle regardless of who fills the now-vacant positions at the White House.

Whipple said he believes the president will likely face an "ugly and unproductive" two-year period if the midterms go the Democrats' way.

So, with a mass exodus on the cards at the Oval Office and the midterms looming, it seems the US President may be in for some tough times, with fewer allies than ever before at his side.

News.title: Buddhist monk ‘punched in the face’ by balaclava-clad boy in UK park
News.content:
Buddhist monk ‘punched in the face’ by balaclava-clad boy in UK park

Karucha Sripramote, known locally as Monk Kom, says he was walking through a park when a thug started spinning his bike wheel to spray dirt on him - before the situation escalated quickly

View 3 Images Karucha Sripramote has lived in Newscastle for more than six years (Image: Karucha Sripramote)

A Buddhist monk was hit with a "rapid flurry of strikes" to his face when he was attacked by a balaclava-clad thug riding a bike in a UK park.

‌



Karucha Sripramote, known as Monk Kom by locals in Newcastle, said he was "repeatedly harassed" by a boy on an electric bike during a walk through Hebburn Riverside Park. After he was shouted at and had his path blocked by the lad on a bike, the situation escalated quickly.

‌



The boy flicked dirt on Karucha with his bike wheel last Tuesday (August 18) before punching him repeatedly in the face. Police are now investigating the attack, reports Chronicle Live.

‌



"He began by sounding a horn behind me and shouting," Karucha recalled. "I was aware of him, but could not hear clearly due to my earphones, so I simply moved aside to avoid his path.

"He then rode in front of me to block my way and continued shouting. I pointed to my earphones and waved my hand to indicate that I had no wish to engage."

View 3 Images Hebburn Riverside Park (Image: newcastle chronicle)

‌



The 34-year-old added: "He then rode closer, turned his bike, and deliberately spun his rear wheel to throw grass and dirt over me. I tried to walk away, but he followed and repeated the action.

"Seeing that he would not leave me alone, I approached him to ask him to stop, but grew concerned he might ride directly at me. I held onto his sleeve to keep distance and reason with him safely, at which point he began punching me repeatedly in the face."

Karucha, who suspects he may have been attacked as he was wearing his orange monastic robes, said he was punched "multiple times in quick succession" and received "a rapid flurry of strikes" to his face before the boy's friend appeared from elsewhere in the park and kicked him with "full force" and knocked him to the ground. He estimates that the boys were between 12 and 15 years old.

‌



Karucha said his glasses were damaged in the attack and he sustained a cut to his lip. He hopes that sharing his experience will prevent anyone else from being targeted.

Karucha said: "Groups of youths wearing balaclavas frequently ride e-bikes dangerously close to pedestrians in this area to intimidate them. It has happened to me before, but this was the first time it escalated to physical violence. My only hope in speaking out is to prevent someone else from getting badly hurt."

He added: "Initially, I intended to let it pass and carry on quietly with my life. However, I realised that staying silent might leave other members of the public, especially elderly residents and families, vulnerable to escalating behaviour."

‌



Since speaking out about his experience, which happened at around 3.30pm on Tuesday, Karucha has been "deeply touched" by the "overwhelmingly kind and supportive" response from the community. He said he has received many kind messages and even flowers from the community.

In an update and heartfelt thank you to the Hebburn community, he shared on the Dhammakaya Meditation Centre of Newcastle Facebook page.

Karucha wrote: "Following my initial post regarding the incident at Hebburn Riverside Park, I thought the matter would quietly pass. Instead, I have been deeply touched by the outpouring of support, warm messages, and today, a beautiful arrangement of flowers delivered to our centre by a kind resident on behalf of the Hebburn community.

‌



View 3 Images Northumbria Police is investigating the incident (stock)

"I am writing this to express my sincere gratitude to everyone and to share a brief update:

"Our Community: I have lived in Hebburn for over six and a half years; I know first-hand how kind, welcoming, and peaceful this town is. This single incident does not change how much I value and appreciate living here.

Article continues below

"Reflections on the Incident: As a Buddhist monk, I contemplate life through understanding, patience, and the principle of cause and effect (Kamma). I hold no anger, resentment, or bitterness towards the young lads. While their actions crossed a line, panic and poor judgement often lead young people to react recklessly."

Karucha said he has "no lasting injuries" and has now "almost completely healed" following the incident. Northumbria Police is investigating the report.

Karucha added: "My only hope is that these young lads take a moment to reflect on the kind of community they wish to grow up in. The way we treat others inevitably shapes the environment our own loved ones and families live in. Thank you all once again for your immense kindness, care, and solidarity."

News.title: Pub and hotel bosses given hope under valuations plan to help struggling industry
News.content:
Pub and hotel bosses given hope under valuations plan to help struggling industry

The Treasury has enlisted an expert to review how business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels and make recommendations for reform of the system

View 2 Images The Treasury has enlisted an expert to review how business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels and make recommendations for reform of the system (Image: Richard Pohle/The Times/PA Wire)

Pub and hotel valuations will be made fairer under plans to make the system more transparent.

‌



Both the pubs and hotels sectors saw significant increases in rateable value at this year’s revaluation in large part due to the ending of pandemic-era valuations. People are concerned that the current system does not reflect the realities of the pub and hotel market, the Treasury admitted.

‌



The Treasury has enlisted an expert to review how business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels and make recommendations for reform of the system.

‌



Jerry Schurder, former business rates policy lead at advisory Newmark UK, will lead the independent review into valuations and report back to the Treasury by the end of March 2027.

A Call for Evidence, which launches on Monday, will ensure landlords, brewers, hoteliers and business owners are properly represented in the process, ministers said.

View 2 Images Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healy at a pub in Essex after announcing a 20% cut in business rates last month (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The government last month cut business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues by 20% from April next year.

The move was largely welcomed but there were calls to apply the relief to a wider range of businesses and to go further with broader changes to the system. No 10 has said it will look to set out further reform, including small business rates relief, at the Budget.

The Mirror is campaigning for more support to protect Britain's struggling boozers.

‌



Financial Secretary to the Treasury James Murray said: “Pubs and hotels are vital for communities and bringing growth to every postcode.

“Last month we announced tax cuts for pubs to give them the breathing room they need. Today we’re going further with a rethink of valuations – so that we can build a fairer system for the future.”

Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the British Beer and Pub Association, said: “For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome.”

‌



Neal Jones, EMEA president at Marriott International, said “The current valuation methodology creates a significant burden for hotels, and it is right that the system is being examined to ensure it is fair, transparent, and reflective of today’s market realities.”

Allen Simpson, chief executive at UK Hospitality, said: “Business rates remain a significant burden for hospitality businesses and the system needs to better reflect the trading realities for the sector. Comprehensive review and reform can address these challenges, while also supporting investment and growth.”

Braden Saunders, UK Spirits Alliance spokesperson and owner of Battersea-based Doghouse Distillery and Bar said: “The Prime Minister’s business rates cut for hospitality costs £100 million.

Article continues below

“The excise duty hike at the last budget lost the Treasury nearly the same amount in spirits revenue last year. Cut excise duty on spirits, fund the rates cut – it pays for itself. We welcome this review and look forward to engaging.”

News.title: Families of two police officers killed in crash say they were heroes
News.content:
Two police officers who died when a car travelling the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into their vehicle have been hailed as heroes by their families.

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died when a Volkswagen Passat, which officers had been pursuing until seconds before, collided with their marked armed response car on the A66 near Middlesbrough on Saturday.

The Passat's occupants - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17 - also died.

In tributes released by Cleveland Police, PC Clough's family said he had been "willing to help anyone", while PC Blades' wife described him as "loved beyond words".

"No words will ever feel like the right words to honour our Matt," she said, adding that he had been a "beloved husband" and the "most devoted father" to their two young sons who would grow up knowing what an "incredible" dad he had been.

"He gave his life in the line of duty, protecting and serving others with courage, dedication and selflessness," she said.

"The pain of losing him is beyond words, and our lives will never be the same.

"Neither will the love he gave us ever fade.

"He may have left this world committed to the duty he believed in, but his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave to his family."

She ended the tribute to her husband: "Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever our superhero. Our Matt and Dad."

News.title: How easy is it to find an NHS dentist? It depends where you live
News.content:
Sykes says that none of his friends in his graduating class in dentistry still works in the NHS. "My friends have gone private, retired or teach - any pathway to avoid NHS dentistry."

Shiv Pabary, chair of the British Dental Association's General Dental Practice Committee, says the situation is "the direct result of choices made by successive governments". He warns that unless ministers "fix and fund NHS dentistry", more dentists could choose to reduce their NHS work or leave the service altogether.

Overall dentist practice numbers have risen in England over the last decade.

"This is not a shortage of dentistry but a shortage of NHS dentistry," says Dayan. "Practices will need to be incentivised back into NHS work in the places where the NHS footprint has thinned most."

While most parts of England recorded declines in practices offering NHS dental care, the reductions were smallest in North West London, the Black Country and North East London.

North East London was the only area to see any increase during the period, recording one additional practice offering NHS treatment compared with a decade ago.

Every other region of England saw the number of NHS dental practices fall.

Looking at the number of practices doing NHS work is not the same as looking at exactly how much health service capacity there is - practices can vary in size. But if you look at other measures such as the amount of treatment being done, the numbers are still down, although not as steep as the fall in practice numbers.

The government says that it is changing the dental contract and training more dentists in the areas most in need. The government says it will also make it a requirement for newly qualified dentists to practice in the NHS for a minimum period of at least three years.

Campaign group 38 degrees calls the current dental crisis "shameful", with people being "forced to pay money they can't afford or suffer with the pain, shame, and further complications that come from being denied vital NHS healthcare".

News.title: Reform says it will prioritise British-born young workers for social housing
News.content:
Reform previously announced it would evict foreign nationals from social housing - a plan criticised by housing charity Shelter which said building more homes is the solution, rather than "changing the order of the queue" and "stoking division".

Tice will set out how Reform intends to pay for the 50,000 affordable homes during Monday's news conference, the party added.

"It is time for us to prioritise young British workers, and that is what our policy is about," Tice said on Sunday.

"I have spent my entire career in property development, as a private citizen I have led companies which delivered thousands of new homes. In government I will break down the barriers to getting generation rent onto the housing ladder."

He added it is "time to get Britain building" and give "our young people the homes they deserve".

UK or Irish nationals made up 88.5% of main social home householders in 2024/25, according to the English Housing Survey.

That means around 11.5% of main householders, the perÂ­son in whose name the social home is renÂ­ted, were non-UK or Irish nationÂ­als.

For its part, Reform estimates 540,000 social homes are currently occupied by foreign nationals.

Labour rubbished Reform's plans and insisted social housing is already "tightly controlled".

"Illegal migrants, asylum seekers and migrants on student or work visas are not eligible for social housing," the Labour spokesperson said.

Labour said the Reform plan would target long-term UK residents that have contributed to our country but are not British citizens, including NHS staff.

"It would leave more families at risk of homelessness and drive up use of temporary accommodation at the taxpayers' expense. It would also mean renegotiations with the EU, resulting in years of wrangling."

The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.

The Tories have said their plan, which would allow Irish citizens and some EU nationals to remain in social housing, would free up around 230,000 homes.

Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing. Now Reform are trying to catch up.

"We also believe in a home owning society and that those who work hard should be able to buy their own home, without unnecessary barriers standing in their way."

Liberal Democrat spokesperson Gideon Amos said that Reform's plan was a "cruel gimmick".

News.title: Pubs and hotels could see business rates reformed after review
News.content:
A review is being launched into the way business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, and could lead to a reform of the system.

The Treasury says business rates expert Jerry Schurder will lead the review into rate valuations and report back in March 2027, with the government calling for the views of landlords, hoteliers and business owners to feed in to the process.

Last month, Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, to come into effect in April.

Pub groups have argued they face disproportionately higher rates bills, but other businesses have called for a wider reform of the rates system.

According to the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), 161 pubs closed in the first three months of this year across England, Scotland and Wales, equating to the loss of around 2,400 jobs.

Rising business rates are cited as one issue facing the sector, although there have also been complaints that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made staff costs more expensive.

James Murray, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the new review would look at "a rethink of valuations - so that we can build a fairer system for the future".

Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: "For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome."

The BBPA says pubs are valued differently for rates than retail venues. Instead of being based just on floor area, they are judged by a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade - which means when a pub's turnover increases, so does its rates bill.

Schurder is a former business rates policy lead at advisory firm Newmark UK, and his review will feed into the next rates revaluation in 2029.

His appointment was welcomed by Craig Beaumont of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) who said he would bring "crucial heavyweight business rates expertise into the Treasury".

However, Beaumont said the government needed to address the wider business rates system and exempt more smaller firms by increasing the rates relief threshold for small businesses.

Tom Ironside from the British Retail Consortium also welcomed the review but said it was "vitally important that the needs of retailers are not overlooked".

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the review was "far too late for a sector this Labour government has already done its best to kill off".

"Tax hikes on business premises and jobs, alongside job-destroying regulation in the Employment Rights Act, have left many hospitality businesses on the brink," he said.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said reform of business rates was "long overdue", but also called for an emergency VAT cut and a reverse to jobs tax changes "which have hammered hospitality in particular".

News.title: Trump waves green flag to start IndyCar race through Washington streets
News.content:
US President Donald Trump was among hundreds of people who gathered to see the IndyCar race through the streets of Washington DC on Sunday, marking the culmination of a series of summer events to celebrate the country's 250th birthday.

Driver Kyle Kirkwood won the race, earning his seventh career Indycar win.

Ahead of the race, the president and First Lady Melania Trump took a ceremonial lap of the 1.7-mile track in his presidential limousine, The Beast.

As they reached the finish line, Trump's new Air Force One completed a flyover above the capital.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is the first time professional road racing has been hosted in the capital.

News.title: CrossCountry to run full train service after power outage causes major disruption
News.content:
Train operator CrossCountry says it expects to run a full service on Monday after cancelling nearly all of its UK services the day before following a power cut at its control centre.

The outage in Birmingham at the weekend brought disruption from Glasgow to Penzance.

Major routes were affected between Birmingham and Manchester, which pass through Stoke-on-Trent, Coventry and Wolverhampton. Journeys from Leeds to York and Cheltenham to Cardiff were also caught in the travel chaos, leaving passengers frustrated.

On Monday morning, CrossCountry reported a handful of service cancellations, although these were put down to trains departing late and staff shortages.

Customers are advised to check their journey before travelling.

The operator on Sunday thanked passengers for their patience and understanding during the disruption.

Tickets purchased for travel on CrossCountry services on Sunday will be valid for travel on CrossCountry services until Wednesday, the company has said.

News.title: Viral 'Cat in the Hat' TikTok trend sparks fun fake videos but also real fear
News.content:
"He's so scary!" says 16-year-old Skye, recoiling at the mention of the Cat in the Hat.

Viral images purporting to show a life-sized version of the Dr Seuss character on the streets after dark have sparked fear and confusion among teenagers.

The posts, seen by millions, have convinced some young people that the character is real and that they might encounter it, prompting police forces in Ireland and the UK to issue statements confirming that the images and videos are fake.

"I was having a sleepover," Skye elaborates, "but everyone started watching Cat in the Hat videos. It was 3am. I wanted to go home. When I started walking down my friends' driveway, I got totally freaked out that the Cat in the Hat was going to jump out. I had to call my mum to pick me up."

A quick scroll through TikTok reveals numerous accounts, many of them created in the past few weeks, sharing photos and videos of an elusive black-and-white feline wearing the famous, towering, crooked red-and-white striped hat.

One post showing the original Cat in the Hat costume, accompanied by the caption "Help, what do I do?", has received 14.6m views in just three weeks.

The comments add to the sense of frenzy, with followers asking, "Why is he taxidermied?" Others zoom in on parts of the costume and post conspiracy theories about Mike Myers, who played the character in the 2003 film, being trapped inside.

Another popular account set up this week, posts videos of a real person dressed in a cat in the hat costume, dancing, with captions like "Kent I'm coming. lock your doors." Other users are sharing the videos, adding their own captions and locations across the UK.

Many of the AI generated images have been centred on the Irish counties of Limerick and Wexford, where shaky videos purportedly showed the character wandering through the streets, causing alarm and confusion among residents.

In Wexford, the local GardaÃ­ (police force) quickly dismissed the sightings as fake and confirmed that the images had been generated using artificial intelligence.

News.title: Doctors said I was too young to have endometriosis at 13 - I had to take morphine to cope
News.content:
But the most frustrating thing for Grace, and why she contacted BBC Your Voice, is because she does not feel medical experts recognise that teenagers and adolescents can suffer from endometriosis.

Grace's GP did not diagnose her condition and nor did the first consultant she saw privately.

She says: "Even a specialist didn't believe me. And if a specialist won't listen to me, who will?" It was not until the family pushed for a second private opinion that she got a positive diagnosis.

Endometriosis, which occurs when tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside it, can cause debilitating symptoms, such as pelvic pain, heavy periods and fatigue. About 10% of women are affected by it, according to NHS data.

This week BBC presenter Emma Barnett revealed she had to have a hysterectomy for her endometriosis - which she said she never wanted to have.

It can develop at any age once periods begin - and it is a common misconception that only older women suffer from the condition, says the charity Endometriosis UK,

Faye Farthing, a spokesperson for the charity, says the government, NHS and health practitioners need to improve menstrual health education for young people "if we are to ensure the next generation are not robbed of the future they deserve".

The charity says it can take a long time to diagnose endometriosis - an average of nine years in older women.

And in the early stages, for example with teenagers, it often doesn't show up on an ultrasound scan. However, new tests are being developed which will help spot the condition earlier.

Getting pregnant can be more difficult - even aged 14, Grace says she has been warned it is likely to affect her fertility. She's been advised she may not be able to have children after the age of 30 because of damage to her reproductive organs.

She feels rushed: "I have to have kids within the next 15 years, otherwise I might not be able to."

News.title: Rain to return this week with chance of thunderstorms and flooding
News.content:
The weather is set to turn more unsettled this week as rain returns with a chance of thunderstorms and localised flooding.

Some places could see a return to showery conditions by Tuesday, but it is from Wednesday onwards that more widespread and persistent rain will arrive from the south.

The wet weather will be welcome for parched regions of the UK, but a lot more will be needed before drought conditions start to ease.

Temperatures will also be on the rise once more, as warmer air moving in could push midweek highs close to 30C (86F) in places.

News.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
News.content:
Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.

The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.

Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.

Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.

"The person who bought Justin's old family home said they'd discovered six sacks of letters, scripts and other material pertaining to Robin Hardy and The Wicker Man in the attic," says Dominic, an art historian at the University of Quebec in Montreal.

"Justin's first instinct was to burn them, but we couldn't ignore this original source material. Although we left it unopened for six months or more."

News.title: 'It's not Alton Towers' - rows break out over queuing at Wales' highest mountain
News.content:
Visitors to Wales' highest mountain are being urged to respect others by not skipping queues to reach the top following rows among climbers.

Recent hot weather means there have been bumper summer crowds at Yr Wyddfa, also known as Snowdon, where people have reportedly waited more than one hour to reach the 1,085m (3,560ft)-high summit.

Social media videos have shown arguments among queue-jumpers and those patiently waiting their turn to touch the metal plate that marks the top.

A recent video showed Marc Screeton, from Manchester, being heckled as he bypassed the line, saying: "Imagine queuing on a mountain? No chance."

But others have said queuing is necessary for safety reasons.

The mountain's growing popularity in Eryri National Park, also known as Snowdonia, has led to bottlenecks, and queues are now common on the stone steps leading to a metal plate or trig point where people pose for photos and videos.

Speaking to BBC Wales, walkers on the mountain had mixed views about those jumping the queues.

Lucy Taylor said: "I think you should queue because it's really quite dangerous and everyone's trying to get up there - it's just not safe."

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool united in tribute to legend Keegan
News.content:
Kevin Keegan's family were in attendance as Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters came together to pay tribute to the former England captain.

Keegan, who played for both clubs, before going on to manage Newcastle, died at the age of 75 last month following a battle with cancer.

As the teams met for the first time since his death, in their Premier League season opener at St James' Park on Sunday, members of Keegan's family were present in the directors' box.

A number of Keegan's former players from this memorable first spell in charge of Newcastle, between 1992 and 1997, were also at the game.

News.title: Scammers increasingly using QR codes to steal money and data
News.content:
When Les Howard could not find change for parking during a trip to the coast, a quick response (QR) code on the meter seemed to be the answer.

But the next day, the 61-year-old realised he had become the victim of an increasingly common scam as criminals started taking money from his bank account in Â£60 chunks.

Reports of QR code-related scams have gone up by 700% in the past four years, figures by Report Fraud have revealed.

Experts say criminals are finding different ways to exploit the codes as they become a common part of everyday life.

This could be disguising suspicious links in emails, gaining access to victims' messaging apps or convincing people who are out and about to download fraudulent apps to steal their money and data.

That is what happened to Howard, from Widnes, who was visiting Caernarfon in North Wales with his wife.

"We went to the car park where we normally go," Howard told the BBC Scam Secrets podcast.

"I normally have change in the car to pay for the parking, but this time I didn't.

"So there was a QR code to download and get an app and pay via an app."

News.title: Mayors to get powers to overrule local councils on planning decisions
News.content:
Mayors across England will be given new powers to overrule local councils on some planning decisions.

The change would apply to proposals with more than 150 homes, more than 15,000 square metres of commercial space or buildings over 30 metres.

Mayors in 13 areas including Manchester, Liverpool, the West of England and the West Midlands will gain similar powers to Sir Sadiq Khan in London, who is already able to "call in" planning decisions.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the powers were an "essential part of the toolkit that mayors need to effectively deliver new homes and regeneration".

The Conservatives questioned whether it was right for councils to lose the "ability to make planning decisions in their own communities".
