The powers will also be available to mayors in the Combined Authorities in North East England, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, York and North Yorkshire, Hull and East Yorkshire, Greater Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, East Midlands, and Tees Valley.

Paul Bristow, the Conservative mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, told BBC Breakfast that if he had local powers, he would approve "tomorrow" a couple of blocked schemes that he said would "get new homes built that families could move into and charge economic growth".

Bristow said "it's not about overriding what local people want", but about developers and councils finding a compromise on projects instead of just saying no - which he believed the "perceived threat of intervention" would help.

In London, where Khan already has the power to review decisions on certain developments, external, housebuilding has fallen in recent years. But Pennycook insisted the "call in" powers had helped the mayor "unblock strategic growth sites" in the capital.

Bristow said if he had a similar local plan it would be "much more light touch" than London.

In the 2024 general election, the Labour government promised to build 1.5 million homes in England by the end of the decade, but housebuilders have warned the target could be missed.

Pennycook said the government was "absolutely determined to stick with that ambition".

He acknowledged the target was "really stretching" but said nearly 180,000 children were in temporary accommodation and "any smaller target wouldn't be commensurate with the scale of the challenge".

Bristow said the government has "no chance whatsoever" to meet its 1.5 million target.

"We need economic growth in this country, we need to get building and families need places to live, and at the moment, the planning system just isn't working."

In addition to gaining the new "call-in" powers, mayors are set to be able to grant "up-front permission", which the government says will allow building to begin "without a developer having to apply".

A consultation on how the powers will work is due to be published next week.

The government has sought to stress that local councils will continue to decide the majority of applications and that all decisions must still follow planning rules.

It has also said mayors will get a "bigger say" over how housing funding is spent in their area, with the government directing national agency Homes England to focus on local mayors' priorities.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who served as mayor for Greater Manchester for nearly a decade, has repeatedly expressed his desire to transfer more powers to local mayors.

"Challenge does need to be made to local decision-making and actually it cuts both ways," he told the Sunday Times.

"Sometimes it's the other way round. It's the local authority putting forward something that's unacceptable in terms of the impact on the community. It's a two-way street."

Last month, Burnham promised to give all mayors a share of income tax revenue, saying he wanted to "bring power home" to "every postcode".

Earlier this week, he announced a secondment programme to send high-performing civil servants to work in mayoral offices.

The approach has faced criticism from some in his own party and the Liberal Democrats, who fear it could create a "two-tier system" that discriminates against those areas that do not have an elected mayor.

News.title: Restriction zone scheme for offenders to start in October
News.content:
A scheme that could see serious sexual and violent offenders confined to areas just a few miles wide after leaving prison will be launched in October, Justice Secretary Alex Norris has announced.

Government ministers say this is designed to give victims greater freedom and further reduce the possibility of unwanted contact

The intention to introduce "restriction zones" for violent offenders who leave prison and who are on probation was first announced by the government last year.

Probation officers will be able to limit where serious offenders can go for as long as it is deemed necessary. Those who breach their new boundaries could be recalled to prison.

This would go beyond the current practice of imposing "exclusion zones" which ban offenders from specific locations such as a victim's home or place of work.

Norris is expected to come up with proposals to further restrict the early release of some prisoners when Parliament resumes next month.

But the Conservatives say that the best thing Labour could do to protect victims is to bring forward emergency legislation which would stop the early release of thousands of criminals.

There is a risk that serious sexual and violent offenders and victims could encounter one another outside exclusion zones.

The new scheme will specify confined areas for offenders in plans tailored to them and developed in consultation with victims.

Norris said the scheme would use GPS technology monitored by probation officers so that "those who step outside the boundaries can be quickly identified and face being sent back to prison".

"Offenders should carry the consequences of their crimes, not their victims," he added.

Amy Glover, director of domestic abuse services at Advance, a charity supporting women and girls who have experienced domestic abuse, praised the "change in focus".

However, she also called for reform to the criminal justice system saying many survivors of abuse chose "not to pursue a criminal conviction, and for those that do only 5% reach conviction."

A domestic abuse survivor named only as Kristina called the restriction zones a "fantastic concept" but noted that a perpetrator had continuously breached her indefinite restraining order "without consequence".

"The biggest challenge would be to gain victims' confidence in authorities to follow through their promises of protection," she added.

The announcement of the restriction zone scheme's start date comes after a change to the government's early release scheme following a backlash.

Introduced to ease prison overcrowding, on 4 August the policy was updated so people sentenced for rape, serious child sex offences and grooming would not be eligible for early release.

The Prison Governors' association warned this change to plans at a "very late stage" put further pressure on prison staff.

The restriction zone scheme was criticised when it was announced last year for potentially putting pressure on probation staff, something the government says it hopes to alleviate with more staff and a greater use of technology.

If you are suffering from domestic abuse, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

News.title: 'My skin makes me unique and I'm learning to embrace it'
News.content:
A woman born with a rare genetic skin condition that covers 98% of her body in birthmarks has spoken of how she is learning to embrace her appearance after years of trying to hide it.

Laura Kelly, 28, was born with congenital melanocytic naevus (CMN) and underwent 14 operations as a baby, with doctors fearing she may not live beyond the age of eight.

Laura said CMN made her self conscious about how strangers might react and that, growing up as a teenager, she often wore heavy makeup and planned outfits to cover her skin.

She said embracing how she looks and raising awareness of CMN has given her more confidence and hopes sharing her story will help others with a visible difference.

The government has told TikTok and other social media companies to take down content featuring a social media trend showing people driving the wrong way down roads.

Defence minister Luke Pollard said social media platforms should act to remove posts.

He told BBC Radio 5 Live: “We’ve communicated to those social media platforms that have been hosting content that celebrates this type of dangerous behaviour on our roads to take down that content.

“I think we all need to give the police time, but there’s also things we can be doing in the meantime to make sure that the internet is a safer place for everyone, that doesn’t celebrate and load views and therefore financial incentives on people to generate such awful content.”

He added: “I want to see social media companies step up.

“It’s one of the reasons they’ve argued against some of the regulations, saying they can police themselves. Well this is the perfect opportunity to demonstrate it. Remove the content that celebrates dangerous behaviour on our roads.

“While that content is online, the government will be using the powers in the Online Safety Act to compel the platforms to take it down.

“But if the social media platforms were to regulate themselves and remove it in the first place, not allow their algorithm to share this type of content, because they know exactly what type of content that algorithm is designed to share, then I think we’d be in a better place.”

More follows on this breaking news story...

News.content:
'Hugely disappointing': Carrick reacts to Man Utd's loss at Hull

Arsenal are hoping to secure the signing of Julian Alvarez to cap off a productive summer of incomings and boost their forward line as they look to defend their Premier League title. Andy Burnham has promised Britain is “100 per cent behind” Ukraine as he arrives in Kyiv on his first foreign trip to mark the country’s independence day.

The prime minister is to chair his first meeting of the coalition of the willing as he arrived in Kyiv on Monday morning to signal Britain’s continued support for Ukraine.

He was pictured shaking hands with Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, and other officials as he stepped off the train.

It comes as relations between the Kremlin and Downing Street continue to suffer amid Vladimir Putin’s ongoing war on Ukraine and threats from Moscow.

But Mr Burnham is set to assure Ukrainians of the UK’s backing and reiterate that Russia’s threats only strengthen British resolve.

“On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes,” he said.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham is set to assure Ukrainians of the UK’s backing and reiterate that Russia’s threats only strengthen British resolve ( AFP/Getty )

“I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine’s security is our security.”

Mr Burnham added: “The friendship between our two countries will long outlast Russia’s illegal war. In both the fight and in the rebuilding to come, we will stand with Ukraine and deliver opportunities for people across both our countries.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

Earlier this month, Russia’s embassy to the UK said reports that Ukrainian forces had used unmanned aircraft manufactured by two UK companies “confirm that London is deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis”.

It accused Britain of “seeking to contain Russia and inflict maximum damage on it by proxy” and warned that the deeper its involvement becomes, “the higher the price it will pay”.

“London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” it said.

As well as chairing a meeting of the coalition of the willing, Mr Burnham will take part in Independence Day events and accept an award on behalf of the British people recognising the UK’s support.

open image in gallery Mr Burnham welcomed President Volodymyr Zelensky to the UK during his first weeks in office ( AFP/Getty )

The government has agreed to allow defence firm MBDA to release classified information on UK components for the long-range Scalp missile – the French-produced version of the UK’s Storm Shadow.

Both missiles use shared French and British technology, and Ukraine and France are looking to set up local assembly lines for Scalp missiles in Ukraine.

His visit marks his intention to continue Britain’s long-standing support for Ukraine, with every prime minister except Liz Truss having visited the country since the war with Russia broke out.

Sir Keir Starmer, who set up the coalition of the willing, visited Ukraine on his final foreign visit as prime minister, where he said the UK’s “cast-iron” support of Ukraine will “always endure”.

Meanwhile, relations between Moscow and Downing Street remain sour, with Mr Burnham having hit back at the Kremlin’s threats.

open image in gallery The government has agreed to allow defence firm MBDA to release classified information on UK components for the long-range Scalp missile – the French-produced version of the UK’s Storm Shadow ( Reuters )

Asked what his message to Putin was after Russia accused the UK of escalating the war, Mr Burnham said: “This is the UK doing what it has long said it would do, which is to support Ukraine 100 per cent against this illegal war led by Vladimir Putin.

“We are providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself, and that’s been the British position all the way through this conflict by previous prime ministers.

“It remains the case with me. We are not fair-weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.”

The Kremlin is also yet to put forward a replacement candidate for its ambassador to the UK after Andrei Kelin left his post in London in recent weeks.

The charge d’affaires has taken the lead, an embassy spokesperson told The Times, raising questions about whether Russia is seeking to downgrade its diplomatic relations with the UK.

One person has died and hundreds have been taken ill following an outbreak of food poisoning across the country.

According to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the wave of salmonella infections "may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK".

The agency confirmed one fatality associated with the outbreak. Salmonella typically triggers self-limiting gastroenteritis, with common symptoms encompassing diarrhoea, stomach cramps, fever, and vomiting.

However, 38 per cent of those affected in this outbreak required hospital admission, and two individuals suffered potentially life-threatening infections in their bloodstream.

Is it still safe to eat eggs?

The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has told the BBC that vulnerable groups should not consume eggs that are runny or under-cooked while dining out.

It said this includes those under the age of five, over the age of 65, pregnant women and anyone with underlying health conditions.

Vulnerable groups should avoid certain foods containing raw egg that are made fresh, such as mayonnaise or souffle. However, eggs that have been well-cooked are fine to consume when eating out or ordering takeaway.

It comes after the FSA said that there is “no evidence that UK-produced eggs are affected”. The standards agency said that investigations had identified links to imported eggs “mainly used by food service and catering establishments such as restaurants or cafes, as a potential source”.

Jacquelyn McCormick, head of incidents at the FSA, says advice around eating eggs remains the same.

She said: “Eggs which are thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically should not present a food safety risk.”

Is there anything I should check when buying eggs?

The FSA says that infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults are advised to only eat runny or raw eggs if they have a British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain egg assurance scheme.

However, people who are severely immunocompromised and require medically supervised diets should follow their doctor's advice.

Anyone handling eggs, eggshells or egg packaging should always wash their hands thoroughly with warm water and soap and dry them properly afterwards.

How many cases have been reported?

Between 11 August 2025 and 1 August this year, 207 cases were identified: 199 in England, six in Scotland, one in Wales, and one in Northern Ireland. London registered the highest total among English regions with 47 confirmed cases, while Yorkshire and the Humber recorded 38.

People affected include babies and people as old as 90, according to the UKHSA.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the salmonella outbreak ‘may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK’ ( Getty Images )

Hannah Charles, lead epidemiologist for gastrointestinal infections at UKHSA, said: “We’re working with Food Standards Agency and other public health agencies to investigate a salmonella outbreak that may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK.”

What are the symptoms of salmonella?

Salmonella generally causes a mild illness, although vulnerable groups with weakened immune systems may experience more severe illness.

Symptoms of food poisoning include:

feeling sick or being sick

diarrhoea

tummy pain

a high temperature

feeling generally unwell

The symptoms usually start within a few hours or a few days of eating food that caused the infection.

Ms Charles said: “Anyone who is concerned about symptoms should contact their GP or out of hours service in the first instance.

“Salmonellosis is often caused by eating or handling contaminated food and can be spread rarely from person-to-person.

“There are simple steps to prevent the spread of salmonella: wash your hands thoroughly after using the bathroom and before preparing and handling food, cook food thoroughly, and if you have any symptoms, avoid handling food for others where possible.”

The news comes as cases of salmonella poisoning after eating contaminated food has hit a decade high in England.

Dr Kimon Andreas Karatzas, professor in food microbiology at Reading University, told The Independent that the cost of living crisis could be behind the rise in cases.

“The cost of living crisis might be potentially driving changes in supply chains. It is possible that the cost of living crisis forces more people to prepare food by themselves, which might increase the chances of cross-contamination,” he said.

He added: “The fact that there is no major increase in salmonellosis infections associated with outbreaks and a concurrent increase in Campylobacter cases [highly associated with cross-contamination at home] might be pointing to this direction.

“A better investigation of the above factors, such as the numbers of salmonellosis infections associated with outbreaks or individual cases, might help us understand what the reason for this salmonellosis increase.”

Motoring experts have calculated which day of the upcoming bank holiday weekend is set to be the busiest on the roads.

They have also identified a number of likely congestion hotspots, including motorways in Gloucester, Somerset and Hertfordshire.

The RAC says that 20 million leisure trips will be made by car between Friday 28 August and Monday 31 August – a bank holiday in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

This represents the largest total recorded since the motoring services company began evaluating drivers’ summer bank holiday travel plans in 2015.

The RAC warned that the coming Friday is “likely to be mired in traffic”, with 4.1 million getaway journeys predicted.

A further 3.8 million leisure trips are anticipated on Saturday, 3.1 million on Sunday, and 3.4 million on Monday, when day-trippers compete for space on the roads with people returning from short breaks.

open image in gallery Traffic queuing for the Port of Dover in Kent during the bank holiday getaway in May ( Gareth Fuller/PA Wire )

An additional 5.5 million journeys will occur across the four-day period, with drivers unsure which exact day they will hit the road.

Transport analytics company Inrix also identified a number of likely congestion hotspots, including:

The M25 anticlockwise from Junction 17 in Hertfordshire to Junction 12 in Surrey, and clockwise from Junction 15 in Buckinghamshire to Junction 19 in Hertfordshire

The M5 south from Junction 15 near Bristol to Junction 23 in Somerset

The M1 south from Junction 16 in Northamptonshire to Junction 6 in Hertfordshire

The M5 north from Junction 11 in Gloucestershire to Junction 1 in the West Midlands.

An RAC survey of nearly 3,000 UK drivers indicated that 13 per cent have scrapped their bank holiday travel plans because of higher petrol and diesel prices due to the Iran war.

Some 8 per cent said they would still make their journey but save money on other things such as accommodation and eating out.

Filling a typical 55-litre family car with petrol now costs about £89, compared with £74 a year ago.

A tank of diesel is about £100, up from £79 in August 2025.

open image in gallery A 'frantic Friday' is expect on the roads ( PA )

The RAC commissioned research company FindOutNow to conduct the survey of 2,939 UK drivers on 17 August.

RAC breakdown spokesperson Harriet Hernando said: “With record numbers making a getaway over the bank holiday, it looks like Brits are buoyed by the persistent warm and dry weather and are more confident in making plans for the late summer bank holiday weekend – which is quite often a washout.

“Drivers should be ready for frantic Friday and think about setting off before 10am if they can.

“If the warm weather continues, people should be prepared in case they get caught in a traffic jam, by carrying plenty of water.”

Breakdown rescue company Green Flag said the number of callouts it received over the summer bank holiday period last year was 13 per cent higher than the previous weekend.

It warned that many drivers may be overlooking “basic vehicle checks” before long journeys, such as tyre pressures and levels of oil and coolant.

Network Rail is carrying out less engineering work than usual for the bank holiday weekend, but thousands of passengers face disruption when the East Coast Main Line is closed between London King’s Cross and Peterborough on Sunday for digital signalling work.

Impacts from other major work include no trains between Stafford and Wolverhampton on Sunday, and disruption in the Leeds area between Saturday and Monday.

A new daily pill to manage diabetes and assist with weight loss will be available at pharmacies across the UK from Monday.

Pharmacists said that the rollout is “particularly significant” for patients who are unable to use weight loss jabs.

The drug is called orforglipron and is sold under the brand name Foundayo. It was manufactured by American pharmaceutical firm Eli Lilly and was authorised by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) earlier this month.

It is the second GLP-1 pill for weight loss to be made available through UK pharmacies, after Wegovy in July.

The UK is the first country in Europe to approve the pill.

Eli Lilly said that it is working with the NHS spending watchdog, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, on its assessment of Foundayo for a potential rollout on the health service in England.

The new once-daily weight loss pill called Foundayo is now available in the UK ( Lilly Medicine )

The medication is licensed for people with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher, or people with a BMI between 27 and 30 who have at least one weight-related condition.

It can also improve blood sugars in patients with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.

The pill is taken once a day, at any time, with no food or water restrictions.

Dosage begins at 0.8mg, climbing to 2.5mg, 5.5mg, 9mg, 14.5mg, and 17.2mg.

Patients will spend a minimum of one month at each dosage level.

“We’re pleased that this means there is another oral treatment option for eligible UK patients alongside licensed injectable treatments,” Khalil Asmar, vice-president of cardiometabolic health at Lilly Northern Europe, said.

Henry Gregg, the chief executive of the National Pharmacy Association, said that it is “another significant day”.

“This is particularly significant for patients who cannot or do not want to take an injectable medicine and could make weight loss treatment available to a wider range of patients.

“It is easier for criminals to provide fake, unlicensed or counterfeit versions of oral medications than injectables and patients must make sure they only access weight loss treatments through safe and regulated pharmacies.

“There must now be a redoubling of efforts within government and the NHS to use pharmacies to make sure more eligible patients in clinical need can get weight loss treatments on the NHS, rather than the current postcode lottery that exists for weight management services via GPs.”

So, it’s almost time to plant your spring bulbs – or is it?

With ground still rock hard from the sweltering summer, it may be wise to at least delay planting spring bulbs until rain has softened the earth, experts advise.

“It’s better to wait for the soil to cool a bit more before planting but on the flip side, it’s still good to get into garden centres and choose the varieties you want early while there’s the best selection,” says Ian Clark, Taylors Bulbs marketing manager. “But it’s definitely better to wait for some rain to make planting easier.”

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“Bulbs are at their most dormant at the moment and the most important time for them is late spring/early summer after flowering when they are taking in moisture and nutrients for the following year,” he continues.

“Hot weather earlier in the summer had a small effect on tulip growth but not too serious, more likely that the bulbs haven’t got quite as big as they might have done had they had more favourable growing conditions.”

“Even if you put them in the ground now, they would stay dormant until we get rain anyway, because moisture initiates root growth,” says Ashley Edwards, head gardener at Crocus.

When you come to plant them, plant your bulbs deeper than you would normally, which will expose them to more moisture.

Can you still plant bulbs in pots in early autumn?

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“Pots are different because you’re going to be watering your pots anyway. You could even start bulbs off in pots and then transfer them into the ground when the rain does come,” says Edwards.

Good candidates for pots include narcissi, crocuses and imperial fritillaries, he recommends, along with hyacinths for scent.

Leave tulips until later

Tulips do have a preference to be planted in cooler soil later in the autumn, and it is better to wait if you can, Adam Taylor, director of Taylors Bulbs, advises.

Tulips, in particular, benefit from being planted in November or even December, when there’s less danger they will succumb to tulip fire, a fungal disease similar to grey mould.

Will those left in the ground survive?

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“If spring-flowering bulbs have been left in gardens from last year, I would expect very few detrimental effects particularly with the early flowering types such as crocus, hyacinth and narcissus,” says Taylor.

“They have been dormant throughout this summer and if we have some moisture for them to start rooting when the soil temperature drops, I expect them to come again next spring without significant issue.

“However, in those areas where we experienced the dry weather in late May, it’s possible that any later spring flowering bulbs left in the ground such as narcissus and particularly the type of tulips that can flower perennially (Darwin hybrid, fosteriana and species types), the leaves will have died back quicker than they may normally do.

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“This will mean the plant was under stress at a time when it will have been creating the new bulbs for next year and/or making the flower bud for next spring’s flower.

“It’s slightly possible in some areas and some circumstances that there may be fewer flowers than hoped but nature will recover this for the year after, should we receive more normal conditions next spring.

“In the meantime, planting some fresh bulbs in those areas will only help fill any gaps that may come in next year’s display.”

Edwards adds: “If they are very congested there’s a chance they could dry out and they might come up blind (without flowers) next year.”

As for tulips, some are more resilient than others when they’ve been left in the ground, such as Tulipa ‘Ballerina’ and ‘Queen of Night’, while many parrot tulips are less reliable, Edwards observes.

open image in gallery Tulipa ‘Queen of Night’ (Alamy/PA)

“I think we should be going more towards the species tulips now because they are adapted to heat, they come from Iran, Turkey and those areas of the world and are used to growing in quite mountainous areas. A lot of them are very resilient and they spread as well.”

What about bulbs you’ve stored?

“The hot weather will accentuate any underlying issues in bulbs such as fusarium in tulips and base rot in daffodils, meaning you see it sooner,” says Clark.

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

If you lifted this year’s spring-flowering bulbs after flowering, you need to have stored them somewhere cool to reduce the likelihood of deterioration. If your once-cool garden shed has become a hothouse, it may affect your bulbs, says Edwards.

“Sometimes the garage is better because it is better insulated than sheds,” he points out. “Sheds can obviously get really hot and if the bulbs are shrivelled or you press them and they crumble under your fingers, then they are too dry and not worth planting.”

Bulbs such as alliums, crocuses and daffodils are a bit tougher, he notes.

“Just test them, make sure there’s no mould on them and they haven’t got any powdery fungal diseases. You need to test the firmness of the bulb.”

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

Sports.title: Fans claim Enzo Maresca is COPYING Pep Guardiola after spotting Man City manager’s passionate antics after first game
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE fans have claimed that Enzo Maresca was imitating Pep Guardiola after Manchester City’s Premier League opener on Sunday.

The former Chelsea boss was appointed the successor to Guardiola after his incredible decade-long Prem journey came to an end following the 2025/26 season.



And the Italian tactician managed to get off to a winning start after stunning Bournemouth late on at the Etihad.

The Cherries took an early lead through Marcus Tavernier, but an 84th-minute Marc Guehi equaliser and an injury time winner from Josko Gvardiol reversed the host’s fortunes late on.



But during the considerable post-match celebrations, Maresca was spotted speaking to some of his players in a way that reminded fans of Guardiola’s iconic mannerisms.

The 46-year-old – who wore a suit for the match – was especially animated as he gestured at and put an arm around Rayan Cherki, before leading him away from cameras on the pitch.



Guardiola was also known for his energetic conversations with his own players on the pitch after matches, especially ones that he was frustrated with.

Fans were convinced that Maresca was trying to ‘copy’ his predecessor’s style.

One disgruntled fan of former club Chelsea wrote: “Such a poor attempt trying to mimic Guardiola’s post-match talks with his players. Temu Pep.”

Another added: “He never did this at Chelsea and he never wore a suit on the touchline trying too hard to be Pep.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

While a City fan joked: “I genuinely thought this was a clip from last season.”

It seemed he emulated Pep not just in outfit but in results, with the win snapping Bournemouth’s 18-game unbeaten run in the competition – the longest across Europe’s top five leagues going into the contest.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Jaissle brutally shuts down Schmeichel on live TV after he claims Man Utd are in for Lewis Hall transfer
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE boss Matthias Jaissle shot down Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel’s suggestion Lewis Hall could still leave this summer.

The German head coach got his first point in the Premier League on Sunday in a dramatic opening weekend draw with Liverpool – and Hall gave away a stoppage time penalty.



Dominik Szoboszlai ruthlessly converted to salvage the score at 2-2, but it was Jaissle and Newcastle who impressed the most.

Despite barely being in the job two weeks, the former RB Salzburg head coach had his depleted squad perform admirably on an emotional day at St James’ Park.



And Hall, subject to much transfer speculation over the past few months, was one of the standouts – until his last gasp blunder.

The England defender, who brutally missed out on World Cup selection, fouled Victor Munoz with just seconds to play.

He was gutted at full-time but had kept Liverpool quiet until then.

And Jaissle is determined to keep the ex-Chelsea academy ace in the North East.

When discussing his plans for the rest of the window, Jaissle admitted: “I think it will be a stressful period for the sporting director [Ross Wilson].

“We have some needs, definitely.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He was then urged to say where upgrades would fit in, and started to answer, “Position wise…” before stopping himself.

Schmeichel, on punditry duty for Viaplay, laughed: “You can tell us.”

And Jaissle replied: “Because you ask, I was about to tell you but I [will] keep it a secret.”

He added: “If you are bringing players in, maybe there will also be some players out.”

United icon Schmeichel then interjected to say: “We’re [Manchester United] looking at your left-back.”



But Jaissle gave the idea short shrift, jumping in and grinning as he said: “No chance! No chance!”

Hall, 21, has been linked with a move away from the Toon for a while – and that has only intensified with United’s expected focus on a left-back over the next week.

SunSport understands that the youngster would find it hard to turn down a switch to Old Trafford – but any deal would be extremely expensive.

Newcastle signed Hall from Chelsea in 2023 on loan before making it permanent for £32million 12 months later.



Now he is established as one of the league’s best left-backs, but has seen a host of key team-mates depart when some have questioned the ambition and direction of the Saudi Arabian project.

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon as well as midfield pair Bruno Guimaraes (club captain at the time) and Sandro Tonali.

Last year Alexander Isak joined Liverpool on deadline day.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But reports say Hall is set to be offered an enormous new contract in order to tie him down.

And Jaissle is willing to make him part of a new-look leadership group including Big Dan Burn.

Sports.title: I managed both Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck – here’s why they are the smartest of transfers for Chelsea
Sports.content:
GOLDEN oldies Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck will do what Chelsea legend John Terry did and galvanise Blues’ young guns.

That is the verdict of Prem legend Steve Bruce who managed both the dynamic duo during their Sunderland days — and Terry at Aston Villa.



As far as former Manchester United skipper Bruce is concerned, there is simply no substitute for experience.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso signed midfielder Henderson, 36, and striker Welbeck, 35, from Brentford and Brighton respectively this summer.



Bruce saw first hand the benefits of having a wise old head after luring centre-back Terry to Villa on a free in the twilight of his career in 2017.

The former England skipper was 36 and able to provide vital know-how to the then Championship side to get the club moving in the right direction again.

Bruce said: “The prospect of Chelsea getting Jordan and Danny at their age was deemed daft by some but for me they’re the smartest of signings.

“It’s a bold move but also a very, very shrewd move by Xabi Alonso to bring in two relatively old heads.

“And I wasn’t surprised at all that they’ve been snapped up because I brought in John Terry to do exactly the same thing — bring leadership to a young group at Villa.

“This is Alonso stamping his mark on the club because young players often need the voice of experience beside them. It’s clear Chelsea have recognised the merits of a better blend which bodes well for them.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And after being handed the captaincy by Bruce, JT galvanised Villa and ended up playing 36 games, finishing with a heartbreaking play-off final defeat by Fulham, Chelsea’s opponents in their Prem opener tonight.

Bruce explained: “As well as defensive qualities, I wanted John to influence the players in terms of how to train and what you needed to do to reach the top and stay there.

“And I have to say JT was inspiring — he set standards and was a real breath of fresh air as a role model, and the younger players relished following his example.

“Villa were still fighting back after being relegated and there was lots of doom and gloom.

“It needed someone like JT to show the players the way forward and lead by example on and off the field.



“He brought drive to the dressing room and that’s invaluable to managers.

“In a similar way, Chelsea’s dressing room will look up to Jordan and Danny for what they’ve achieved and the type of pros they are and that will pay dividends.

“It’s a real statement of intent and a priority is clearly to bring stability to his dressing room.

“And there’s no better way to do it than to bring in two of the English game’s finest elder statesmen, so to speak.

“All the young players at Chelsea will look up to these two in admiration and learn vital lessons and they’ll create a feeling of togetherness.



“They have thought the average age of the squad is too much on the young side and Danny and Jordan will redress the balance with experience.

“They’ve gone out and signed two seasoned Premier League campaigners who will lead from the front.

“They won’t play 50 games but they look after themselves, and if they get 25 to 30 games under their belt they’ll have done their jobs.”

Bruce worked with the pair fairly on in their careers.

Henderson was coming through the ranks at Sunderland and Bruce’s United connections got rising star Welbeck to Wearside on loan for the 2010-11 campaign.



And they combined to fabulous effect at Stamford Bridge as Sunderland chief Bruce masterminded a stunning 3-0 win on November 14, 2010.

Henderson caught the eye with a vital assist while striker Welbeck sealed victory late on.

Bruce added: “The reason Jordan got into the first team was based on his leadership qualities, even as a youngster.

“Even though he was just 18, he helped the more experienced players work their way through the challenges of pre-season.

“That ability to lead by example got him in the team and kept him in the team and earned him a move to Liverpool where he won the lot.



“It’s one thing being driven and being a good pro, you’ve also got to have technical ability and he’s shown he’s got it in abundance time and time again for club and country.

“He made the best of his natural ability due to hunger, desire and commitment to better himself. And there’s still that determination to succeed which was there for all to see when he was a teenager.

“His potential was vast and over the years at Liverpool, Jordan proved to be a hell of a signing by Kenny Dalglish.

“You can’t deny anyone the chance to move to a club of Liverpool’s stature and he grabbed the opportunity with both hands and became a mainstay of the side.



“To keep himself in such good nick for so long is down to his desire, which is born in you, and his commitment to his profession.”

Bruce tried to bring in Welbeck when he was Hull boss but he joined Arsenal in 2014.

He said: “I always felt that Manchester United got rid of Danny too quickly.

“He’s got the lot as a forward, two good feet, clever movement, good finishing ability, and what’s key is he seems to be getting better with age.

“He scored 13 Prem goals last season in a good Brighton side and if he stays fit he’ll have a very positive impact.

“Danny’s had a wonderful career and now, like Jordan he’s got the chance to end it on another high.”

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca fires clear transfer message to Man City board after fielding shock lineup in first game for club
Sports.content:
ENZO MARESCA played Marc Guehi as a makeshift midfielder in perhaps a pointed message to Manchester City’s board.

City are on the brink of an £86million deal for Lille wonderkid Ayyoub Bouaddi but Maresca wants more players in the engine room.



Maresca was forced into finding a “solution” after Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders left the club, while Nico Gonzalez is linked with Newcastle.

England centre-back Guehi scored City’s equaliser as new boss Maresca oversaw a comeback 2-1 win over Bournemouth, with Mateo Kovacic on the bench.



Maresca said: “I had to find a solution. I don’t know if Marc can play there for the next game again. Now we need a different solution.

“I know Marc from Crystal Palace and I always thought he could be a good midfielder. So sometimes you visualise things you need to try.”



Maresca revealed he planned to “see the board” following the final whistle, unaware that City were already on the verge of landing Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old, who starred for Morocco at the World Cup, is set to become the most expensive teenage signing in Prem history, beating the £59.9m rivals United paid for Leny Yoro from the same club in 2024.

City, who signed Elliot Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest, want Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez while Adam Wharton of Crystal Palace and Roma’s Manu Kone have also been on the club’s wishlist.

As well as Guehi, Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola this summer, also picked full-back Nico O’Reilly in an attacking midfielder role.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Asked if City have finally tracked down a “new Rodri“, a deadpan Maresca said: “Marc Guehi.” It brought a laugh, but relying on an England defender in central midfield is clearly no long-term fix.

Maresca celebrated his first Prem win as City boss, but admitted plenty of work needs to be done before the window closes on September 1.

The Italian added: “At the moment I don’t have a best XI but day by day I can see more clearly.”

City survived a late scare while a freshly trimmed Erling Haaland had a close shave of his own, drawing a blank on opening day for the first time in his Premier League career.

Maresca revealed Rayan Cherki was “not happy” about being benched — before coming on to deliver an “unbelievable impact” with two assists to spark City’s thrilling turnaround.



Maresca turned to blow kisses at his family in the stands after Josko Gvardiol‘s stoppage time winner was given after VAR overturned the on-field officials offside call.

The former Chelsea boss, who watched as a section of fans unearthed a welcoming tifo at kick-off, said: “It was the perfect day. I was very emotional.

“I was very pleased when the game started to watch the banner on the other side. I was happy at the end because we walked away with three points.”

City forward Omar Marmoush was on the bench ahead of a potential move to Spurs, while Jack Grealish was brought on in the final eight minutes and was serenaded by the home crowd in what could have been his final match for the club, with a return to Everton looming.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Maresca said: “He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best from him. The window is open for one more week and we will see what happens.”



Asked where he will play next week, Guehi jested: “Who knows? Maybe up front. We’ll see.”

Sports.title: Arsenal star Christos Tzolis kicks off derby for his former club and is given hero’s welcome by fans
Sports.content:
NEW Arsenal fan favourite Christos Tzolis “kicked off” for another team just days after his Premier League debut.

The Greek winger, who joined the Gunners for £34million earlier this summer, made the most of some time off following Friday’s 3-0 win over Coventry.



He returned to former side Club Brugge over the weekend and got a standing ovation from fans.

Tzolis, 24, was paraded in front of the Jan Breydel Stadium despite leaving barely a month ago.





And after getting a rapturous pre-match reception, he took a fake kick-off ahead of the Brugge derby.

Played between Club and Cercle, who both have home games at the same ground, Tzolis returned to the stands to watch his ex-team-mates come away with three points.

They won 1-0 and continued their 100 per cent start to the league campaign.

Although still early on in his Prem and Arsenal career, Tzolis has become an immediate hit at the Emirates after a sparkling opening performance and strong pre-season showings.



He spent just two years in Belgium after arriving from Dusseldorf – where he moved following a forgettable spell at Norwich.

And Tzolis was an output machine, scoring 43 times in 108 appearances with 45 assists.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Last season alone he bagged 17 times with a staggering 23 assists in just 36 league outings.

He rocked up in Brugge in a white t-shirt and a giant smile on his face.

Wearing several bracelets on his right wrist, Tzolis had his name sung by the Brugge faithful.



He even shook hands with the ref as Cercle and Club lined up on either side of the pitch.

In baggy black trousers and white trainers, he turned to all sections of the crowd and applauded.

Patting his chest with his hand, Tzolis was given the match ball and placed it on the centre circle.

The ref blew a fake starting whistle and Tzolis kicked it back to Club Brugge and got another big cheer.

He put his arms in the air before heading off the pitch and embracing with boss Ivan Leko.



Tzolis also got a touch from the mascot.

Sports.title: Unai Emery hints Ollie Watkins REFUSED to play for Aston Villa in 4-0 Brighton thrashing amid Al Hilal transfer interest
Sports.content:
UNAI EMERY hinted Ollie Watkins refused to play for Aston Villa.

The Villa boss said he could not explain why Watkins was not in the squad for their rout at Brighton.



Striker Watkins, 30, has been linked with a move to Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal this summer.

The Villans are understood to have knocked back FOUR bids for the England star.



Asked why Watkins was not part of the Villa squad, Emery said: “This question is for him. I can’t answer. I can answer only with my silence.”

Probed whether Watkins is refusing to play, Emery added: “I think you can call him. You can call his agent and he can respond.



“It is not my responsibility. Only his answer can explain. I can’t.

“I can answer about Emiliano Buendia, Ross Barkley, John McGinn.

“But we have had this problem every season and we overcame it.

“It is something we have to accept and we have always reacted.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Before kick-off, Emery replied “silence” when asked if Watkins had played his last game for the club.

Watkins’ absence was coupled with injuries to Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, meaning Emery was forced to play without a recognised striker against Brighton.

Brighton got four in 25 minutes, with Jack Hinshelwood and Maxim De Cuyper among scorers.

Keeper Emiliano Martinez was also absent from Villa’s squad as he edges closer to a move.



Emery has lost Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans from his Europa League winners.

And new £34million buy Joao Gomes is now banned for Villa’s home game against Arsenal next Monday after he picked up a red card for kicking out at Georginio Rutter.

On his team’s poor performance, Emery said: “We made mistakes and they scored their goals.

“In 20, 25 minutes we lost everything and it was a strange, strange moment.



“Conceding four goals is not normal in my four years working here.

“As well, the red card. Emotionally, we lost it a little bit.”

Villa captain John McGinn said sorry to the travelling fans.

He said: “The goals we conceded were poor. We obviously apologise to the supporters.”

Sports.title: Gary Neville makes demand over Liverpool duo after dire displays - 'We've been kind to them'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville makes demand over Liverpool duo after dire displays - 'We've been kind to them'

Liverpool stars Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak both failed to make an impact as the Reds had to settle for a 2-2 draw against Newcastle at St James' Park on Sunday

View 3 Images Gary Neville issued a warning (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has told Liverpool stars Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to 'sort themselves out' and justify their huge price tags. The Reds duo were among the weakest performers for Andoni Iraola's side, who needed a stoppage-time penalty to snatch a 2-2 draw away to Newcastle in their opening Premier League game on Sunday.

‌



Isak, who joined Liverpool from Newcastle last summer for a record-breaking £125million, missed two big chances and only had six touches in the opposition box. Meanwhile, £115m signing Wirtz - one of Europe's most sought-after players before his move from Bayer Leverkusen - was hooked on the hour mark after failing to put his stamp on the game.

‌



Both players had difficult first seasons at Liverpool, who sacked Arne Slot in May and appointed Iraola in the hope that the former Bournemouth boss will get the best out of them. But if that doesn't happen, they've been warned that they'll face a pile-on.

‌



Speaking on his Gary Neville Podcast, the Manchester United legend said: "The big thing for Liverpool is they've got this quarter-of-a-billion-pound front two, Isak and Wirtz and bloody hell, we've been kind to them.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"They're going to have to start playing sooner or later or else, to be fair, they're going to get quite a lot of criticism. For a start, they're too nice, and if you're going to be nice, you'd better be incredible at football.

"I don't see the tenacity in Wirtz in particular. I just see a nice player moving around the pitch, not really ever looking like he's busting a gut to do anything.

"Now, that can happen. Sometimes players have that flow about them, but I want to put a rocket up him. I want to put a rocket up him because there's ability there, there's talent there, the understanding of his position.

‌



"The biggest disappointment for me [Sunday] is those two." Neville added: "I've watched them both for 12 months, and I do actually have faith in them.

"I think Isak's an exceptional player and we've seen it. I never saw anybody give Gabriel [Magalhaes] and [William] Saliba or [Virgil] Van Dijk and [Ibrahima] Konate a tougher time as Isak did when he played at Newcastle in a black and white shirt.

Do you agree with Gary Neville? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



3 View 3 Images Florian Wirtz was subbed off against Newcastle (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images) 3 View 3 Images Alexander Isak didn't get on the scoresheet (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

"I've seen him be devastating. Now Liverpool fans and his team-mates and coaching staff, they need to see that - because that's £125m they've spent on him.

‌



"And then Wirtz, he needs to sort himself out. Enough's enough now, we've talked about him enough. He's young and he's come to a different country - and I'm all for willing him on.

"They have both had a bit of a free ride. Obviously Isak was injured last season but Arne Slot loses his job, and Wirtz has played like that, so let's be clear, this has got me to start some real focus now.

"I can see a real player there, but can't keep watching this stuff and he's been subbed after an hour and they need a goal, but they're 2-1 down, so no that's not right."

Both players were left out of PSG's squad for their French Super Cup defeat to Lens last weekend as well as the club's Ligue 1 opener at Rennes on Sunday night.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak's subtle action to Newcastle fans after Liverpool's late equaliser
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak's subtle action to Newcastle fans after Liverpool's late equaliser

Alexander Isak and Liverpool snatched a late point at Newcastle, where the Swedish striker faced a hostile reception on his return to St James' Park

View 2 Images Alexander Isak was public enemy No 1 on his return to Newcastle

Alexander Isak offered a little wink as he left the St James' Park pitch after Liverpool rescued a point at Newcastle.

The Swede was back at his former home for the first time since forcing his exit from the Magpies, and he was widely booed by the home crowd. They jeered his every error but the striker was able to celebrate a late equaliser with his team-mates.

Dominik Szoboszlai's penalty in the 99th minute made the game 2-2 late on, denying Newcastle the three points. Isak led the line for Liverpool but found it hard to impact the game. The forward's best chance came in the second-half when he fired in a shot from the edge of the box.

It blazed over, with the Newcastle fans taking great joy in cheering his miss. Isak was able to avoid losing on his return to Newcastle and offered a wink after the final whistle, reports the Chronicle.

Given the acrimonious nature of his exit from the north east Andoni Iraola admits he knew a hostile reception was coming from those who used to cheer his name.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Liverpool boss said: "I think he expected a little bit the atmosphere, I don't think [it] has been a big surprise for him. I think he has tried everything, has given us good positions on the ball.

"[He] probably has had a couple of situations to finish inside the box, but probably not the clearest that he wanted or we wanted, but I value that. He has continued pushing on in the game, fighting, and I think it's a good step for Alex for being the first game."

Once Liverpool were awarded the stoppage time penalty attention turned to who may take it, especially with Mohamed Salah now gone. Isak was a contender but in the end Szoboszlai stepped up, and hammered home emphatically.

View 2 Images The Swede had struggled to impact the game on Sunday afternoon

Iraola insists Liverpool could go in a number of directions with their penalty taker, but praised the quality of his Hungarian midfielder. He said: "I think we have not only Dom and Alexander [Isak] – we have more very good specialists. Alexis [Mac Allister] also was on the pitch and he's a very good penalty-taker, Cody – we have a lot. But I think Dom showed the level. It's an almost impossible penalty to stop.

"I was happy obviously because at the end we recovered one point. I also think there is a clearer penalty before the Victor [Munoz] one to Victor again, but I think the referee whistles just before, so they cannot give it to you, but I think it was even more clear than the second one. I'm happy also for Victor because he has created problems to his opposition and I think these players from the bench that can alter games are going to be important for us."

Sports.title: Diego Simeone addresses brutal Julian Alvarez jeers as Arsenal target blockbuster transfer
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone addresses brutal Julian Alvarez jeers as Arsenal target blockbuster transfer

Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move away from Atletico Madrid and the Arsenal target was booed by his own fans during the 2-2 draw with Villarreal on Sunday

View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez. (Image: (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Diego Simeone says it was planned that Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez would not stand with his teammates to show appreciation to Atletico Madrid supporters after the full time whistle on Sunday. The forward was jeered off the pitch by his own fans and had to be escorted down the tunnel by club staff after Atleti's 2-2 draw with Villarreal.

‌



Alvarez forward has been heavily linked with a departure from Simeone's squad throughout the summer transfer window. The club turned down an approach from city rivals Real Madrid at the start of the window, before Barcelona made their intentions clear that they were keen to snap up Alvarez.

‌



The former Manchester City star has made no secret of his desire to leave the club, publicly declaring his wish to join the reigning La Liga champions. However, Atleti have stood firm in their refusal to sell to their domestic rivals, leaving Alvarez increasingly frustrated.

‌



Gabriel Martinelli poised to hand Arsenal huge payday as £60m transfer option emerges READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez 'contacted' by Mikel Arteta as Arsenal transfer response given READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alvarez was named amongst the substitutes for the 2-2 draw with Villarreal, entering the fray in the second half to a chorus of boos from the home faithful. He played his part as ten-man Atletico fought back to salvage a point, yet was met with a hostile reception from his own supporters throughout his time on the pitch.

Alvarez was led down the tunnel by staff while his teammates went over to applaud the supporters at the final whistle. As he departed the pitch, Alvarez was once again subjected to jeers and whistles, casting further uncertainty over his future at the club.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal continue to pursue a transfer for Julian Alvarez (Image: (Photo by Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

Addressing the situation, Simeone said: "It was a club decision to not let Julian Alvarez go over with his teammates to greet the fans."

Ahead of the match, the Atleti manager said: "For me, Julian is an extremely important player for us to achieve our objectives. As long as he's with the team, I'm going to look after him."

‌



Arsenal are believed to be strongly interested in securing the striker's services as they look to strengthen Mikel Arteta's squad. The Gunners are aiming to defend their Premier League title and go one step further by lifting the Champions League trophy.

Landing Alvarez would send out a powerful message of intent, and according to reports emerging from Spain, Arsenal could be the sole remaining route for the Argentine frontman should he wish to depart the club.

Alvarez's remarks about joining Barcelona have sparked a fierce backlash, with posters appearing around Atleti's training ground on Friday morning reading "JULIAN FUERA" ("JULIAN OUT") and featuring the striker's No. 19 crossed out.

Sports.content:
Alejandro Balde gives transfer green light as Man Utd handed huge Barcelona boost

Manchester United are looking to sign a new left-back this summer, with Barcelona's Alejandro Balde emerging as a potential target

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde could be on the move (Image: Alex Caparros, Getty Images)

Manchester United have seen a significant boost in their bid to snap up Alejandro Balde from Barcelona. While the Red Devils are thought to see Lewis Hall as an ideal successor to an ageing Luke Shaw, Newcastle United's determination to hold onto the youngster is proving difficult.

‌



It has been reported that the Magpies will only facilitate a departure for the 21-year-old should United cough up a fee surpassing Lucas Hernandez's record-breaking £68million move from Bayern Munich to Real Madrid in 2019.

‌



As a result, United have started to look further afield for reinforcement to their defensive backline. Barcelona's Balde is considered a potential candidate to fit the bill.

‌



The 22-year-old has been at the Catalan club since coming through their youth academy in 2021. However, owing to fierce competition for places and injury setbacks, he has recently fallen out of favour in Hansi Flick's thinking.

Wayne Rooney blasts one Man Utd star for 'schoolboy' level in Hull embarrassment READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford sends Man Utd message after dismal Hull City loss READ MORE :

According to Sport, the Spaniard has given Portuguese super-agent Jorge Mendes the green light to source him a new club. Balde has been left out of Flick's first-team squad for their La Liga opener away at Elche on Sunday evening, with the head coach making clear he only wishes to call upon players who are 100 per cent committed to the club.

As a result, United could secure a bargain alternative to Hall in the coming days. Nevertheless, the Red Devils will face stiff competition for the full-back's signature, with clubs in Portugal and Italy also understood to be keen.

‌



It follows United's apparent focus on bolstering their midfield following Casemiro's departure on a free transfer, with several new arrivals at the heart of the engine room and potentially more additions on the horizon.

View 2 Images United have also taken a keen interest in Newcastle full-back Lewis Hall (Image: (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



United snapped up Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa in a £35m deal, before securing Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £52m. The club are also targeting Brighton and Hove Albion's Carlos Baleba, a year after interest in the 22-year-old first emerged.

United have struck a £70m agreement for the midfielder, inclusive of £5m in add-ons, with a five-year contract on the table for the youngster - who missed the Seagulls' Premier League curtain-raiser against Aston Villa on Sunday through injury.

It comes as United will be looking to make amends for a 2-0 defeat to Hull City on Saturday when they welcome fellow Premier League newcomers Ipswich Town to Old Trafford in seven days' time.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca dodges early Man City question as late show spares his blushes
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca dodges early Man City question as late show spares his blushes

MANCHESTER CITY 2-1: BOURNEMOUTH: Enzo Maresca was facing an embarrassing defeat on his first Manchester City outing before two late goals as the Italian seeks to fill the huge void left by Pep Guardiola

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca's Man City tenure began with a win

Had Pep Guardiola masterminded this comeback win, he would have been hailed a genius again. But Enzo Maresca still has a long, long way to go before earning comparisons to the bloke he has replaced.

‌



In the meantime, Maresca will just be relieved to have got his first positive result on the board, however difficult it was to get. For more than 84 minutes Manchester City appeared to be heading towards the kind of defeat which would have raised serious questions about Maresca's ability to fill the gigantic shoes of Guardiola.

‌



Marcus Tavernier had put Bournemouth ahead before half time, sending most of the Etihad into silence. And despite dominating possession, City offered little in the way of a fightback, aside from some bad misses from Erling Haaland and Marc Guehi.

‌



But thanks to bit of luck and the introduction of Rayan Cherki, Maresca's men somehow snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Guehi's deflected header from Cherki's corner levelled the scores, before Cherki's clever pass allowed Josko Gvardiol to snatch the winner in stoppage time. And breathe, Enzo.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Fresh off a thrashing from Arsenal in the Community Shield, City begun their league campaign knowing the visit of Bournemouth carried a bit more significance. Starting with a home defeat to a team you'd trounced by an aggregate score of 34-6 in nine previous home wins, was unthinkable.

‌



Not least when Maresca had rolled the dice and picked two of his stars in unorthodox positions, with Guehi operating as a defensive midfielder and Nico O'Reilly starting in the No.10 role. Visiting boss Marco Rose was also starting a new job, and handed a debut to Antonio Silva following his arrival from Benfica.

City started well and ripped into Bournemouth. Haaland tore through midfield to help create a chance for Rico Lewis, but his shot was well saved by Dorde Petrovic. O'Reilly had a free header from the resulting corner, but sent it onto the roof of the net, before Phil Foden had a shot blocked.

View 2 Images Josko Gvardiol scored in stoppage time to down Bournemouth

‌



Haaland then blew a golden chance, fluffing a cross from O'Reilly after the England international had charged half the length of the field before picking him out to perfection. The blunder looked even worse on 26 minutes, when Rose's men went ahead.

It was their first real attack of the game, but a clinical one. City failed to deal with a long ball forward, allowing Rayan to turn sharply and pick out Evanilson, who delivered a sublime cross which Tavernier converted at the back post. Cue silence in most parts of the ground.

It took a crucial interception from Gvardiol to stop Rayan from having a clear run on goal, as City continued to wobble. Petrovic scrambled to his left to keep out a header from Haaland, but the visitors were looking the most dangerous. Tavernier curled a strike just wide and Gianluigi Donnarumma did well to deny Justin Kluivert.

‌



A rumpus on the stroke of half time summed up City's frustrations. That feeling got worse when Guehi missed an absolute sitter from close range, when it looked easier to score.

City needed a spark and Guehi provided one, equalising with five minutes remaining to make amends, before Gvardiol completed the fightback. But it could still promise to be a long season for Maresca. Provided he survives to the end of it, of course.
