World.title: Africa: The Deadly Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak Can Be Stopped
World.content:
Dr Mohamed Janabi (WHO Regional Director for Africa -left), Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (WHO Director-General - center), and Dr Jean Kaseya (Director-General of Africa CDC -right) at a press briefing in Kinshasa during a joint high-level mission to Uganda and DRC on 4 and 5 August 2026.

guest column

Each time we travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), we first go to listen.

In Bunia, we have met dozens of community representatives: survivors, women, young people, local organisations, health workers and leaders from affected areas. Their message is direct: involve us. We know our communities. We know where families seek care, how information moves and why trust is breaking down. Give us the means to help drive the response. They are right.

Ebola spreads through communities, and communities hold the knowledge required to stop it. They can identify illness early, alert health teams, help identify and trace contacts, challenge dangerous rumours and support families through access to treatment and safe, dignified burials. The response always moves faster when communities lead alongside national authorities and health workers.



Communities are not just part of the response. They are at its heart." - Tedros

One hundred days ago, the Government of the DRC declared the country's 17th Ebola outbreak following confirmation of the Bundibugyo virus. WHO subsequently declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, followed by Africa CDC's declaration of a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security.

Priorities are clear: reach every affected area, protect frontline workers and turn commitments into action.

The scale of the emergency is immense. As of 21 August 2026, the DRC has reported 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths across 56 health zones. This is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak recorded, and it is moving faster than any previous one. It is being fuelled by insecurity caused by decades of armed conflict that have undermined law, order and social services and displaced more than a million people.

At the centre of the response are the people who show up every day. Health workers care for patients. Laboratory teams identify the virus. Contact tracers follow its path. Community health workers build trust where fear and misinformation have taken hold. Burial teams help families honour their loved ones safely and with dignity.

They are working under extraordinary pressure, often in insecure and hard-to-reach areas. Some have contracted Ebola in the line of duty.

Their service must be met with action: safety, protective equipment, training, sufficient medical supplies, timely payment, psychosocial support and access to rapid diagnosis and high-quality supportive care if they fall ill. The safety of frontline workers is central to stopping transmission.

The response has made progress. Under the leadership of national authorities, Congolese responders, WHO, Africa CDC and partners have expanded surveillance, deployed laboratories, supported treatment centres, reinforced infection prevention and delivered essential supplies.

Uganda has interrupted locally acquired transmission of the virus. Several health zones in northern Ituri province and South Kivu have also interrupted transmission. These experiences prove that the outbreak can be stopped more quickly when rapid detection, decisive national leadership and close cooperation with communities break the chains of transmission. But the continued emergency in Ituri and five other provinces demands urgently scaled up action.

To turn the corner, surveillance teams are being expanded and equipped to detect cases early and rapidly identify contacts. Safe clinical care and infection prevention measures are being increased wherever people seek treatment. More risk communication and community engagement teams are being deployed to reach out to communities to empower them to participate in the response and address barriers to care. More safe and dignified burial teams are working to prevent transmission associated with deaths. Special efforts are being made to reach vulnerable populations and communities in insecure and hard-to-reach areas.

But despite all these efforts, more is needed. We need to scale our response by two to three times current capacities, across all the response pillars.

Front-line workers' safety is essential to stopping Ebola.

Health facilities require urgent protection from infection. As of 20 August 2026, 158 health workers have been infected and 45 have died. Every facility in an affected or high-risk area needs trained staff, protective equipment, clean water, sanitation and functioning infection-prevention systems.

National and local teams need predictable funding for surveillance, laboratories, treatment, logistics, infection prevention and community engagement. Frontline workers must be paid on time. Local organisations need direct support to work consistently with communities. Supplies must arrive before stocks run out.

Delayed financing costs lives. Fragmented financing leaves gaps. Ebola exploits both. On the ground we at WHO and Africa CDC have established tight integration among health and relief organizations working with the government. Donors therefore need to support and enhance that integration, rather than support siloed and disconnected efforts.

Cross-border also coordination must remain strong. People move within and between countries to trade, work, study, seek care and support their families. Borders must serve as bridges for coordinated public health action. This does not require closing borders or imposing blanket travel and trade restrictions. Such measures can disrupt response operations and livelihoods without stopping transmission.

Close 

The priority is coordinated surveillance, rapid information-sharing and prepared health services along movement routes. Find every case. Follow every contact. Break every chain of transmission, protect every health and frontline worker, save lives and ensure that no community is left behind. Bring testing, and treatment closer to every affected community. Bolster cross-border coordination. Scale up international support. Turn every pledge into action.

African leadership and international support are necessary.

WHO and Africa CDC will continue working with the DRC, neighbouring countries, communities and partners to deliver on these priorities. Our responsibility is to bring the full strength of international and continental cooperation behind the nationally led response.

Uganda and areas in DRC have shown how the course of the outbreak can be turned, through rapid detection, decisive action and close cooperation with communities. But these measures must be delivered at scale. Success depends on sustained national leadership, continental solidarity and international support. We must rise to this challenge, together.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is Director-General of the World Health Organization. Mohamed Yakub Janabi is Regional Director of the World Health Organization African Region. Jean Kaseya is Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

World.title: Somalia: Mogadishu's 'Forced' Eviction Turns Into War
World.content:
The demolition of homes in Tookiyo neighbourhood, in Mogadishu's Yaqshiid district, has triggered tensions and clashes between government forces and local residents who opposed the operation. The demolitions began around midnight and were still continuing, with local reports saying nearly 10 people had been injured in the confrontation.

The operation has raised concerns among residents over the fate of families living in the area and renewed a wider dispute over land ownership and evictions in parts of Mogadishu. Residents say they have lived in Tookiyo for decades and are demanding clarity over the legal basis for the demolitions.

Government forces were accompanied by workers carrying tools used to dismantle the corrugated iron roofing of homes, according to residents and local reports. Several houses occupied by civilians were reportedly targeted during the operation.

Tensions escalated when some residents attempted to prevent the demolitions. The confrontation reportedly led to violence between the security forces and residents, with reports of gunfire in the area.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Local sources said nearly 10 people were injured in the clashes, including civilians. Reports of fatalities have also circulated, but the number of deaths has not been independently verified.

Residents said they were particularly concerned about families who could be left without shelter if the demolitions continue. Some said they had lived in the neighbourhood for many years and had no immediate alternative accommodation.

One resident said the community wanted authorities to clarify who legally owns the land before homes are demolished, arguing that families should not be removed without a clear legal process and adequate consideration for those affected.

The Somali government has not yet issued an official statement specifically addressing the operation in Tookiyo or the reported injuries. Local reports have, however, linked the demolitions to wider efforts by authorities to reclaim land considered government property.

The developments come amid continuing disputes over land ownership and evictions in Mogadishu, where residents in several areas have raised concerns about demolitions and displacement.

The situation in Tookiyo remains tense, with residents worried that further demolitions could lead to additional confrontations and displacement.

The immediate challenge for authorities is how to resolve the dispute over the land while preventing further violence and protecting civilians who live in the affected area.

World.title: Somalia: Somalia Says It Is Aware of Military Operations Off Puntland Coast
World.content:
Mogadishu, Somalia — Somalia's federal government is aware of military operations and shelling off the coast of Puntland, the state minister for defence said Saturday, amid growing concern over attacks linked to a resurgence of piracy.

State Minister for Defence Omar Ali Abdi told reporters in Mogadishu that if military operations were being carried out against pirate groups off Somalia's coast, the federal government was the legal authority responsible for authorising such actions.

"The federal government is aware of the incidents, and a comprehensive report will be submitted," Abdi said, without identifying the forces involved in the reported operations.

He said the government was preparing a detailed report on the incidents and would take measures to address the escalating situation.



His comments came hours after Puntland authorities demanded explanations over shelling they said was carried out by unidentified international warships off the region's coast on Aug. 18 and 20.

Puntland said the attacks had targeted fishermen and damaged civilian property, raising concerns over the safety of residents in coastal areas.

The Puntland Ministry of Security and Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration said it was particularly concerned about the potential impact of military operations in the Garmaal area, near coastal locations where vessels seized by pirates are reportedly being held.

The ministry warned that such operations could harm civilians who have no involvement in piracy and undermine cooperation between Puntland security agencies and international partners involved in efforts to combat maritime crime.

The latest developments come as Somali piracy has made a comeback after years of relative decline, with several commercial vessels seized in recent months in the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean.

Puntland authorities have previously said they were investigating information suggesting that forces outside the regional administration could be involved in the renewed piracy, but they have not publicly identified any group or country or provided evidence to support the claim.

The incidents have also raised questions over the role of foreign military forces operating against pirate groups in waters off Somalia.

The reported shelling follows the burial on Thursday of four suspected Somali pirates in Garmaal, in Puntland's Nugaal region, after what local sources described as a Turkish strike.

The men were reportedly killed when a small boat carrying individuals allegedly linked to the hijacking of a commercial vessel was targeted.

Close 

Relatives of the deceased blamed Turkey for the strike, but Turkish authorities have not publicly confirmed or commented on the reported operation.

Somalia's federal government has been seeking to strengthen coordination with international partners as it confronts the renewed piracy threat, while also asserting its authority over military operations conducted in Somali waters.

The government has not publicly disclosed details of the reported foreign operations or said which forces were responsible for the shelling.

The latest dispute comes at a sensitive time for Somalia, where authorities are trying to suppress piracy while avoiding civilian casualties and maintaining cooperation with international maritime security partners.

The Defence Ministry's promise of a comprehensive report could provide further details on the circumstances surrounding the operations and clarify the respective roles of the federal and regional authorities in responding to the renewed piracy threat.

World.title: Nigeria: Police Rescue 75 Passengers Abducted By Gunmen in Kaduna
World.content:
Operatives of the Nigeria Police Force have rescued 75 kidnapped men, women and children after armed kidnappers abducted them from commercial buses in Birnin Gwari Local Government Area of Kaduna State.

The victims, identified as Fulani travellers, were reportedly intercepted on August 19, 2026, at about 5:30 p.m. by gunmen armed with AK-47 rifles and other sophisticated weapons at Folwaya Village, near Birnin Gwari.

Force PRO, CSP Anietie Iniedu said in a statement that "the attackers reportedly forced the passengers into the forest, where they concealed them inside a cave located in a mountainous area.

"However, their ordeal came to an end after the Kaduna Police Command received credible information from the Birnin Gwari branch of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW). Acting swiftly on the intelligence, a crack team from the Birnin Gwari Area Command was deployed to the suspected location.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The police operatives, who were reportedly well-armed, stormed the area, forcing the kidnappers to flee and abandon their captives.

All 75 victims were successfully rescued unharmed."

Commending the operation, the commissioner of police, Kaduna State Command, CP Rabiu Muhammad praised the NURTW Birnin Gwari branch for its timely and vital intelligence, describing public cooperation as crucial to tackling kidnapping and other violent crimes.

The commissioner also commended the Area Commander, Birnin Gwari, and his operatives for their swift, professional and decisive response, which resulted in the safe recovery of the victims.

CP Muhammad urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to the police, stressing that timely intelligence could save lives and frustrate criminal operations.

He further warned members of the public against taking the law into their own hands, cautioning that vigilante actions or reprisals could escalate violence and result in the loss of innocent lives.

World.title: Kenya: Ruto Warns Against Leaders Peddling Hate, Ethnic Division
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto has taken aim at politicians who he says are using tribal rhetoric to divide Kenyans.

Speaking in Taita Taveta, Ruto said Kenya needs political leaders who can bring citizens together rather than exploit ethnic differences.

"There are some politicians who are not very intelligent. They come here and divide the people. They bring hatred, they bring divisions, and they say these are cousins, these are traitors, these are betrayers, those are enemies. That is outdated politics. Such people should not even be leaders, whether of a village or even a cattle-dip chairman. Those are useless people," the President said.

Ruto questioned whether Kenyans elect their representatives based on tribe or on the work they have done.

"Let me ask you: when you elect a leader, do you judge them by their appearance or by their work? Do you judge them by their tribe or by their work? Do you judge them by the intrigues they engage in or by their work?"

"Let them build railways, build roads, build markets, build housing, take children to school and ensure people receive healthcare and are able to pay for it. That is the scorecard," Ruto asserted

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo and M23 Rebels Agree On Roadmap for Peace in Eastern Congo
World.content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the M23 rebel group have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks aimed at resolving the protracted conflict in eastern DRC. It marks the latest step in an internationally brokered peace process that has seen the parties make cautious concessions, without ending the fighting.

Following talks in Switzerland earlier this week, the parties have committed to "pursue negotiations towards comprehensive peace", mediators said in a joint statement released on Saturday night.

They staked out a roadmap "setting out sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations" and agreed to establish a mechanism to address problems implementing the peace deal they signed late last year in Qatar, the statement said.

They also affirmed "the importance of a standardised method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations".



A ceasefire verification mission is due to arrive in Minembwe, in South Kivu province in eastern DRC, on Monday. The highland region has seen fierce fighting in recent months as militias allied with M23 and the DRC government battle for control.

It will be the first formal inspection since the peace deal was signed in November 2025, and the first deployment of the shared body meant to oversee it.

Slow peace process

The latest negotiations took place in Switzerland from 17-21 August, mediated by the United States, Qatar, Togo, Switzerland and the African Union Commission.

The agreement the two sides signed in Doha last year aimed to lay the foundations for a comprehensive peace deal, setting out commitments on prisoner exchanges, humanitarian access and restoring state authority.

But fighting has continued and disagreements remain over issues including territorial control and the transfer of detainees.

In one of the first concrete steps in implementing the agreement, earlier this month Democratic Republic of Congo authorities released 15 prisoners and handed them over to M23 and its political wing, the AFC.

DR Congo hands first prisoners back to M23 rebels under peace deal

Decades of conflict

For decades, armed groups have battled for control of eastern DRC and its valuable natural resources, which include minerals critical to the world's electronics industry.

The conflict has intensified in the past five years as M23 launched a new offensive. The rebels succeeded in seizing swathes of territory last year, including Goma, the capital of North Kivu province.

Close 

The fighting has killed thousands of people and displaced millions.

The DRC, the United Nations and several Western governments have accused Rwanda of backing M23 with troops and weapons, but Kigali denies the allegation.

Goma's residents reflect on life a year after DR Congo city fell to M23 rebels

In turn, Rwanda says an armed group active in the eastern DRC, the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) - which is linked to the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi people - constitutes a major security threat, and accuses the Congolese government of failing to dismantle it.

The US brokered a separate peace deal between the DRC and Rwanda last year. The DRC agreed to disband the FDLR, while Rwanda promised to withdraw its forces and end its alleged support for M23.

Yet Washington accuses Rwanda of maintaining troops in eastern DRC and has imposed sanctions on the Rwandan army, as well as companies accused of trafficking minerals from areas controlled by M23 rebels.

World.title: Kenya: Mystery Elephant Deaths in Kenya Leave Experts Divided Over Cause
World.content:
Conservationists and Maasai communities are calling for urgent answers as paralysis-like symptoms spread among elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park, with competing theories emerging over what is causing their deaths.

A mysterious ailment has killed at least 20 elephants in southern Kenya since June, alarming conservationists and local communities as experts struggle to determine the cause of the deaths.

The latest victim was an 11-year-old male known as Genghis Khan, who was found lying on the ground in the Kitenden B reserve near Amboseli National Park, unable to stand and struggling to breathe.

Veterinarians tried to revive him with a glucose injection - one of the few options available while the cause of the illness remains unknown - but he died on Tuesday after repeatedly trying and failing to get back on his feet.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The deaths have affected mostly females and young males, with the animals displaying strikingly similar symptoms, including weakness and partial paralysis.

The incidents are particularly sensitive in the Amboseli ecosystem, a major wildlife destination overlooked by Mount Kilimanjaro across the border in Tanzania. Its elephant herds are one of the region's biggest tourist attractions, making their unexplained deaths a concern both for conservationists and for communities whose livelihoods depend heavily on tourism.

"You would find one struggling for a day, struggling for two or even three days. Until they completely die," said Patrick Papatiti, head of operations for the Olgulului communal lands, which include the Kitenden B reserve.

The growing number of carcasses has added to concern among conservationists.

At one site, the remains of a four-month-old calf lay partly eaten by hyenas and covered in flies. Elsewhere, vultures fed on the carcass of a pregnant elephant that had died close to giving birth, along with her unborn calf.

Conservationists in Kenya pay tribute to the late 'super tusker' Craig

Poisoning suspicions

In late July, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said toxicology tests had detected high concentrations of cyanide in the elephant carcasses, raising the possibility that the animals had been poisoned by pesticides linked to nearby farms.

But a number of local wildlife experts and conservationists have dismissed this theory.

Papatiti, who grew up in the local Maasai community, believes the elephants are suffering from a disease rather than poisoning. He said there was "no way" cyanide could explain the pattern of deaths.

One reason for the scepticism is the apparent absence of deaths among other animals who have come into contact with the carcasses.

Scavengers including hyenas, vultures and insects have continued feeding on the remains without showing obvious signs of poisoning - something local observers say would be unusual if high levels of toxic chemicals were responsible.

"If another animal feeds on that carcass and it is not dying, then definitely it is not a chemical," said Joel Nyika, Amboseli ecosystem manager for the Kajiado County authorities.

Nyika also questioned suggestions that naturally occurring cyanide in vegetation could be responsible, arguing that if that were the case livestock grazing in the same areas would most likely also have been affected.

"As wildlife managers, we believe it could be a disease that is only affecting these elephants," he said.

Paula Kahumbu, conservationist and head of Wildlife Direct, said there was still too little evidence to support the pesticide theory.

She also noted that relatively few adult males had died, despite the fact that they are the most likely to enter farmland and raid crops - behaviour that would theoretically expose them more to agricultural chemicals or deliberate poisoning.

Close 

Papatiti has also rejected the idea that farmers are intentionally poisoning elephants.

Hundreds of elephants die in Botswana in mysterious circumstances

However, the KWS said the evidence gathered so far does not point towards an infectious or transmissible disease. In a statement on 7 August, the wildlife authority said its findings had not indicated a contagious illness and sought to reassure visitors that travelling to the area remained safe.

Rather than looking for individuals to blame, Papatiti said, the priority should be establishing exactly what is causing the animals to fall ill.

He believes more elephants may have died without this being recorded and is concerned that similar cases could be occurring across the nearby border in Tanzania, part of the same wider ecosystem used by roaming herds.

"How many elephants will die before we can stop this?" he asked.

(with AFP)

World.title: Enes Kanter Freedom opens up on confrontation with Natasha Cloud that led to ejection, WNBA pursuit
World.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud made a vulgar remark toward him and repeatedly cursed before security removed him from Sunday night’s game against the Indiana Fever.

Freedom, who was sitting near the baseline at Wintrust Arena, said the confrontation began after he celebrated a 3-pointer by Fever guard Sophie Cunningham.

"Sophie Cunningham shot a three, and I put my hands up to celebrate," Freedom said. "Literally, a couple possessions later, Natasha came back and started screaming and yelling and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’

ENES KANTER FREEDOM MET WITH HOSTILE WNBA FANS EN ROUTE TO FEVER-SKY MATCHUP

"And I was like, ‘I am not trying to sleep with her. I’m just here to protect women and support her.’ And then, obviously, after that she started yapping, and she started to walk towards me, and literally I just got up, and then I was like, ‘I’m just here to protect women, and that’s all.’"

Video of the incident showed Cloud walking toward Freedom, yelling and pointing at him late in the third quarter. Freedom stood, extended his arms and took a step onto the court as security and Sky players moved between them.

Freedom said Cloud then began using profanity in front of young fans.

"She started to yell. She started to use some very heavy language. She started to actually cuss, and I was very shocked that there were a lot of kids and that there were a lot of teenagers at that game," Freedom said.

"I just cannot believe that she was just cussing and using those F-bombs in front of all these kids. I’m sure she’s loved in Chicago and many kids are idolizing her and stuff, but that’s not how a WNBA athlete should react."

The confrontation came with 1:22 remaining in the third quarter, after Cloud scored inside and celebrated with teammate Aicha Coulibaly. Cloud then turned and approached Freedom, who was wearing a black shirt that read, "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

He said he believes the shirt contributed to Cloud’s reaction.

"I was cheering for my friend Sophie because when she shot that three, I put my hands in the air," Freedom said. "A couple possessions later, she came back and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’ And I was shocked. I was like, ‘Listen, I’m not trying to sleep with her. I think she’s awesome. She’s a good friend.’ But I think it has a lot to do with my shirt.

FORMER NBA STAR ENES KANTER FREEDOM WRITES LETTER TO WNBA OFFICIALLY DECLARING FOR 2027 DRAFT

"I was obviously wearing a shirt explaining what a woman is, and I think that had a lot to do with what she thinks about women. I think it triggered her a lot."

Cloud sent a message to the trans community after the game, in a post on Threads.

"To every trans kid/person, You are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me," Cloud wrote.

OutKick reached out to Cloud's rep for further comment.

She wasn't made available during the team's postgame press conference.

Sky coach Tyler Marsh defended Cloud after the game, telling reporters, "We all embrace her as someone who protects our team and protects people who need to be protected."

Freedom said security approached him and ordered him to leave without providing an explanation.

"I was like, ‘Can you please tell me why I need to leave?’ They said, ‘Look, you just need to leave,’" Freedom said. "They pretty much pushed me to leave the gym."

However, Freedom insists the words exchanged with Cloud and had nothing to do with the issue of transgender people or his plans to compete in the WNBA.

"Definitely not," Freedom said of the interaction being related at all to those issues.

Footage showed arena staff touching Freedom and sharing intense words with him as he was being escorted out. Freedom said he asked an arena employee not to touch him as he was escorted away from the court.

"I told her, ‘First of all, please don’t touch me because I didn’t do anything wrong. I can get myself out of the game,’" he said. "And the second, I was like, ‘Do you guys realize that you guys are only kicking me out of this game because I support women and I try to protect women?’"

Freedom said security again declined to give him a reason for his removal.

"They were like, ‘Listen, we can’t give you any reason right now. Just leave, please,’" he said. "I played 11 years of basketball in the NBA, and I know how tough the security’s job can get. So I didn’t want to make their job even tougher."

OutKick reached out to the Sky and Wintrust Arena for comment.

The Sky had advanced notice that Freedom would be coming to the game, according to him. He said his manager had notified Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca before the game that he planned to attend.

"My manager texted the GM of the Chicago Sky," Freedom said. "We texted him and said, ‘Hey, just so you know, we are coming to the game. We’re not here to cause any kind of drama. We’re not here to cause anything bad. We are just here to watch the game and leave in peace.’ My manager texted the GM, and he said, ‘Enjoy the game.’ That’s it."

Cloud met with team and league security after the game but did not speak to reporters.

The Fever defeated the Sky 113-90. Clark scored 37 points, while Kelsey Mitchell added 30.

Freedom attended a rally in support of Cunningham outside the arena before the game. Cunningham has faced protests and counterprotests since saying she opposes transgender girls and women competing in female sports divisions.

Freedom announced earlier this month that he intends to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. He has said he is using the league’s rules to challenge the WNBA to clarify its eligibility standards.

The WNBA’s collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," but it does not publicly define the term or establish specific eligibility requirements for transgender athletes. No transgender woman is known to have played in the league.

After Freedom and former NBA player Royce White announced their intentions to enter the draft, the WNBA said its anti-hate task force had discussed transgender athletes and online attacks against players.

"There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others," the league said in its Aug. 12 statement.

Freedom rejected the characterization of his campaign as anti-transgender or anti-LGBTQ.

"I want to make that very clear because, unfortunately, many media organizations and many journalists are making me look like I am anti-trans or anti-LGBTQ," he said. "That is wrong. I respect anyone’s personal decision, and I do respect any kind of group out there."

Freedom said the confrontation made him more determined to pursue a place in the league.

"If anything, I’m more pumped up," he said. "I cannot wait to go against Natasha now. I think it will be fun for me if I get drafted by any other team. I don’t think Chicago will select me. We know that now. But any other team, I just cannot wait to go against her."

Freedom said he has not heard from the WNBA since announcing his plans. He offered to speak directly with WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert.

"If the commissioner of the WNBA wants to sit down and have a conversation with me, I am open to do that as well," Freedom said. "I respect everybody, and I would like to listen to everybody and see what their perspective is."

Freedom said Sunday marked his first time attending a WNBA game in person, although he regularly watched the league during his NBA career.

"I’m obviously a huge fan of basketball, a huge fan of women’s basketball, and I was there to watch the game," Freedom said. "I watched on TV so many times, obviously, but I think this was my first WNBA game ever."

Freedom said he had never spoken with Cloud before the confrontation. Despite their exchange, he praised the veteran guard’s ability and influence on the court.

"I think she’s an excellent player," Freedom said. "I don’t really know what she does off the court, so I can’t really speak about it. But I think on the court, she makes herself better and she makes everyone else better around her, and I think that’s a very special player."

After leaving the arena, Freedom said he encountered a young girl and her mother while preparing to eat dinner. He said their interaction became the most emotional part of his night.

"One of those little girls came with her mother, and then her mother said, ‘Thank you for what you’re doing for my little daughter,’" Freedom said. "I think that was the most emotional part of the whole night."

Freedom said the interaction reinforced his belief that the dispute should not be viewed through a strictly partisan lens.

"This is not a right or left issue," he said. "People need to understand this is not a political issue. This is just common sense. People are trying to make me look like I’m taking a political stance. People are wrong."

Golden State Valkyries player Gabby Williams is the reason Freedom is now pursuing the WNBA, according to him.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"If they don’t come up with a rule, then I am ready and prepared to play in May and just get ready for the draft in April," Freedom said. "These are the rules. People are mad at me. I’m confused why people are mad at me. These are the rules that literally they put, so I’m just literally following their rules."

And The 6-foot-10 former center intends to play well beyond just one season if the league allows it.

"I’m 34 now, and I can go out there and dunk everything," Freedom said. "I watched the game tonight. I feel like every time I touch the ball, I can dunk everything, so the physical advantage obviously is there. I think I can play till 40, 45. I don’t even think there is a limit, as long as I want."

When asked whether he would feel guilty competing against women or entering a WNBA locker room, Freedom said he would not.

"Why would I?" he said. "These are the rules that they set, and I’m just following their rules. All these players, all these coaches and the league itself advocated and encouraged this whole thing. You see all these players come out and say, ‘I will welcome a trans athlete on my team or against my team.’ And the same thing with coaches. You see all these T-shirts that they’re wearing. So, because of that, I would not feel any guilt."

Freedom identified the Fever as his preferred destination and said he would like to play alongside Clark.

"I think we need to bring back the modern-day Kobe and Shaq, so I think I’m going with the Indiana Fever, for sure," he said. "Me and Caitlin will be the modern-day Kobe and Shaq."

White announced his own intention to enter the WNBA draft shortly after Freedom. Freedom said the two former NBA players have never spoken and are not coordinating their efforts.

"He is his own man. I’m doing my own thing," Freedom said. "What Royce is doing is going to affect him, and what I’m doing is going to affect me. So we are two separate people. We’re doing our own thing, and I’m not affiliated with anyone."

However, Freedom said other former professional players have privately expressed interest in following him. He claimed he was communicating with two former NBA players, three European players and three NBA G League players.

"You’ll be shocked, actually, other than one other player that already came out, how many other players I’m actually talking to right now," Freedom said. "There are two former NBA players, three European players and three G League players that I’m currently talking to about this whole thing."

Freedom said the G League players pointed to the potential financial incentive created by the WNBA’s new salary structure.

"The G League players said, ‘Listen, we are only making $45,000 a year. All we have to do is identify as a woman, and we will be making $1.4 million a year,’" Freedom said. "That’s almost a $1.3 million difference. So the WNBA has no idea what they’re about to face."

Freedom also said he has received death threats and abusive messages since announcing his draft plans.

"I do get a lot of death threats and cuss words every day," he said. "I really want people to understand I’m not doing this for any kind of political reasons. This is not a right or left issue. I’m only here to defend women."

Freedom said he has not discussed his campaign with Cunningham or any other current WNBA player or coach. He said no one from the league has contacted him since his announcement, but he remains willing to engage directly with its leadership.

"I’m here to sit down and listen," Freedom said. "If the commissioner or whoever wants to sit down and have a conversation with me about this whole thing, then I would love to sit down and hear her side."

World.title: Suspect in deaths of 5 found dead after cops uncover grim scene at rural property outside Portland
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A man suspected of killing five people in a rural area outside Portland, Oregon, was found dead inside a vehicle in Enumclaw, Washington, on Sunday in an apparent suicide, according to authorities.

Benjamin Charles Parker, 36, was identified as the suspect in a quintuple murder after the bodies of five dead people were discovered on Saturday at a home in a rural community near Forest Grove, Oregon, about 25 miles west of Portland.

"Through their investigation, they believed that Parker was in Enumclaw, WA. Officers from the Enumclaw Police Department located Parker’s vehicle and found him deceased inside. It is believed he died by suicide," the Washington County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement.

The Enumclaw Police Department said that an unidentified was found dead behind a Safeway grocery store in connection with the Forest Grove investigation.

PARENTS FOUND BURIED BEHIND HOME IN WEALTHY NEIGHBORHOOD AS POLICE LAUNCH INTERNATIONAL MANHUNT FOR SON

The Washington County Sheriff’s Office said there is no known threat to the public.

It is unclear how investigators were led to Parker or what connection he had to the victims. Detectives have said they do not believe the killings were random, but authorities have not publicly described Parker’s alleged connection to the victims or a possible motive.

The sheriff's office previously said it responded early Saturday to reports of a vehicle fire at a property in Forest Grove, where the remains of five people and "several domestic animals" were discovered.

Authorities have not released the ages or genders of the victims, how they died or what possible connections they might have with one another. The type of animals found dead at the property was also not disclosed.

Detective Shannon Wilde from the sheriff's office said investigators were still working to determine the victims' identities.

"Any time you have one person deceased, let alone five, that's a logistical challenge," Wilde said, emphasizing the complexity of the investigation and the large crime scene.

Sheriff Caprice Massey encouraged anyone who is familiar with the property or the people who live there to contact authorities with any information they may have.

A California family reportedly filed a lawsuit accusing Six Flags Magic Mountain of a defective ride design after their 22-year-old son suffered fatal head trauma while riding the the X2 attraction.

The incident happened in summer 2022, when Christopher Hawley, a San Diego State University graduate, visited the Los Angeles County theme park with his family, according to Fox 11 Los Angeles. Hawley reportedly collapsed shortly after riding the X2 roller coaster and died the following day.

Separately, the X2 roller coaster was involved in another incident on July 5, 2026, when a rider was found unconscious, prompting the attraction to close for more than a month, KTLA reported.

Christopher’s death was ruled an accident caused by blunt-force head trauma sustained from the attraction, which his family described as exceptionally rough, Fox 11 said.

PANIC AT POPULAR THEME PARK AS STRANDED RIDERS SCRAMBLE TO ESCAPE BROKEN ROLLER COASTER

His younger brother, Alex, described the ride as intensely violent, saying it jerked passengers around before ending with a jolt that sent their heads slamming into the headrests.

"It was very rough. It just jerked us. It just jerked us all around," Alex told the local station.

"It just jolted us all the way forward and then our heads just swung all the way back into the headrest."

After Christopher stepped off the attraction, he reportedly appeared noticeably unwell, with his face turning very red before suddenly collapsing.

Emergency responders rushed him to a nearby hospital, but he succumbed to his injuries the next day, Fox 11 reported.

STARTLING FOOTAGE FROM AMUSEMENT PARK SHOWS THRILL RIDE HALTED AS GUESTS WAIT IN MIDAIR

The family said a surgeon compared Hawley's injuries to shaken baby syndrome, a condition in which violent and sudden forces cause the brain to move rapidly within the skull, potentially resulting in swelling, bruising and bleeding.

"The surgeon had said, he likened it to shaken baby syndrome, that the ride hit his head so hard that it had basically ruptured his brain," Christopher's father, William, told the local station.

Six Flags declined to comment directly on the litigation to Fox News Digital.

However, the amusement park told Fox 11 that the ride remains closed following the separate July 2026 incident involving the unconscious rider.

"The ride remains closed at this time. It has been closed since the evening of July 12th," Six Flags said.

World.title: Sean Grayson, ex-deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey, dies, attorney says
World.content:
Sean Grayson, the former Illinois sheriff’s deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey in her home in 2024 after she called 911 to report a prowler, has died, his attorney said Sunday.

Daniel Fultz, the attorney who represented Grayson during his murder trial, said he died around noon. He was six months into his 20-year sentence for second-degree murder.

Grayson, 32, was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023, and it had progressed to Stage 4 and spread to his liver, lungs and rectum, another defense attorney, Mark Wykoff, said at his sentencing in January. In July, he was denied medical release by the Illinois Prisoner Review Board.

It was not immediately clear whether cancer is what caused Grayson’s death.

Grayson shot Massey, 36, after he responded to her 911 call shortly before 1 a.m. July 6, 2024. The shooting, which was captured on body camera video, set off protests and calls for justice.

Grayson was convicted last year.

During the 911 response, Massey picked up a pot of boiling water from her stove, prompting Grayson to back away, according to court testimony.

Grayson testified that he believed Massey was going to throw the boiling water on him after she said, “I rebuke you in the name of Jesus.” When Grayson looked confused, Massey repeated the sentence.

He testified that he took the remark as a threat.

Grayson pointed his gun at Massey and threatened to shoot her, according to body camera video. She apologized and dropped to the floor, but he fired three times, striking her.

Grayson declined to offer medical care, Sangamon County State’s Attorney John Milhiser said in court. Massey was pronounced dead at St. John’s Hospital in Springfield.

First Assistant State’s Attorney Mary Beth Rodgers said in court: “‘I’m sorry.’ That is the last thing Sonya Massey said before the defendant murdered her, just like he said he would.”

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker signed the Sonya Massey Act, a law requiring stricter background checks for law enforcement hires, and it went into effect at the beginning of the year.

Sangamon County officials agreed in early 2025 to pay a $10 million settlement to Massey’s family.

World.title: Father of sailor aboard USS Abraham Lincoln detained by immigration authorities, family says
World.content:
The immigrant father of a sailor on board the beleaguered USS Abraham Lincoln was detained Saturday by immigration officials, family members said.

Luis Manuel Aviles, originally from Nicaragua, was detained shortly after 11 a.m. ET in Key West, Florida, where he lives, stepdaughter Katty Delgado told NBC News on Saturday evening.

She said that Aviles has been in the U.S. for roughly 20 years and that she has no knowledge of an arrest history or criminal allegations against him.

“He’s doing everything the right way,” she said.

The Department of Homeland Security confirmed Sunday that the Border Patrol arrested Aviles during a traffic stop in Key West. The agency said Aviles entered the U.S. illegally at an unknown date and location and would remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings.

“We are simply enforcing the laws passed by Congress. This Administration does not pick and choose which laws to enforce,” a DHS spokesperson said.

Delgado said she learned the news from family members, including Aviles’ wife and his son Joshua Aviles, who posted a note about the detention on Facebook. Her stepfather, Delgado said, was arrested near a Publix supermarket as he was headed to a mechanic.

Luis Manuel Aviles and his son Joshua Aviles. Katty Delgado

Joshua Aviles said on Facebook that he’s on board the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, which is on its way back to the U.S. after its prolonged stretch at sea, including its deployment to the Middle East to engage in the war with Iran.

“I’ve been deployed for over nine months, out at sea in the Middle East aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, fighting for a country that has given me everything,” he wrote Saturday.

He said that his father is hard-working, giving and humble and that he has a work permit, a Social Security card and a driver’s license.

“This is heartbreaking for me,” Joshua Aviles said. “I don’t know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like a criminal.”

Asked to confirm whether Luis Manuel Aviles had a Social Security number, a work permit or pending immigration cases, as his family indicated, DHS told Telemundo, NBCUniversal’s Spanish-language network, that “work authorization or a pending application do NOT confer legal status in the United States.”

The Lincoln left its home port of San Diego on Nov. 25, and, with more than eight months since it visited a port in December, it broke the Navy record for time without a port call. Relatives of sailors on board the carrier have described reports of deteriorating conditions and morale. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said claims about the situation on board have been “completely misrepresented.”

The Navy said Saturday that the Lincoln has officially left the Middle East en route to the West Coast, a journey that could take a month or more.

Joshua Aviles, who told NBC News he has limited internet access, wrote on Facebook that he’s doing everything he can to get his father released from detention.

“I love you with all my heart. Please stay strong. I’m coming home, Dad,” he wrote.

President Donald Trump has stood by his administration’s immigration crackdown, including ICE’s expanded enforcement and arrests, which in recent months have included the arrests of children and spouses of service members, a San Diego Padres minor-league catching coordinator and a grandmother from India who’s a schoolteacher with a green card.

Immigration authorities have detained more than 50 parents and spouses of service members during Trump’s second term, according to a recent Associated Press investigation. There has been backlash to the detentions, which come despite programs for military members that can sometimes offer immediate family protection from deportation.

The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services website says those “discretionary options” are offered on a “case-by-case basis.”

It was not immediately clear whether Luis Manuel Aviles was in the program.

The DHS spokesperson said in a statement Sunday that “having a family member in the military is not a free pass to violate our nation’s laws.”

“Military service by an immediate relative does not automatically grant parole, lawful status, or immunity from immigration enforcement,” the spokesperson said.

Delgado lamented that her stepbrother has spent nine months out at sea, without seeing his family, “and this is what his father gets.”

World.title: Kyle Kirkwood wins IndyCar race in downtown D.C. celebrating U.S. 250th birthday
World.content:
Reaching top speeds of about 180 mph during the weekend, the cars zipped down Pennsylvania Avenue between the Capitol and the White House, the longest straight on the track. They raced past the D.C. courthouse and the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum on the seven-corner track.

“You can’t even put it in words. This is incredible,” Kirkwood said in a postrace interview. “Man, that was a hard race. One hundred forty-seven laps. I’m out of breath right now.”

President Donald Trump, who joined forces with D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser to launch the race in January on short notice, waved the green flag to start the race. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy waved the checkered flag to end it.

Trump sought to place himself at the center of the action, taking a “lap of honor” in the armored presidential limousine nicknamed “The Beast” ahead of the race and arranging an Air Force One flyover. It was one of seven waves of military flyovers in the preshow, capped with a pass from all six branches of the military with a B-2 bomber as the centerpiece.

To hype the race, Trump hosted numerous events at the White House featuring IndyCar drivers and officials. He posed for a photo on the grid with first lady Melania Trump and several racers.

After it became clear that Congress would reject an originally planned loop around the Capitol because of advertising restrictions on the grounds, Trump issued an executive order green-lighting the modified course.

“We were going around the Capitol, but this turned out to be a better track — and so now we see the Capitol,” Trump told race broadcaster Fox Sports. “You see it right behind you. And I want everyone to be safe, and I want the people to have a good time.”

World.title: Dan Sullivan endorses Dan Sullivan to beat Dan Sullivan in perplexing Alaska Senate race
World.content:
A new Dan Sullivan has entered the conversation surrounding the Alaska Senate race, in which incumbent Dan S. Sullivan faces a candidate with the same name.

The Republican former mayor of Anchorage, Dan A. Sullivan, endorsed GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan for re-election over retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan and Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola on Tuesday.

“As the OG Dan Sullivan, I urge Alaskans to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. He’s been great for Alaska,” the former mayor wrote on Facebook.

Both Dan S. Sullivan and Peltola advanced to the general election in November after the all-party primary last week. The primary is decided by ranked-choice voting, and the top four finishers advance, regardless of political affiliation. NBC News has not yet made a call regarding who the other two candidates will be, but Dan J. Sullivan could be among them.

Alaska’s Senate race is considered one of the most competitive this cycle, when control of the upper chamber hangs in the balance. With primary votes left to count, Peltola so far has 48% of the vote, with Sen. Dan S. Sullivan taking 43%. Dan J. Sullivan — who is running as a Republican — has 2.4%, with other candidates getting considerably fewer votes.

Democrats view the election as a seat they could flip in November. The Cook Political Report rates the race a tossup.

The Sullivan saga has drawn attention as former teacher Dan J. Sullivan’s candidacy has faced legal challenges. Dan S. Sullivan and Republicans have alleged that the teacher was placed on the ballot to confuse voters and detract from the senator’s share of the vote, claiming he’s working with Peltola.

Dan J. Sullivan has denied coordinating with the Peltola campaign. Peltola has also denied any involvement with the second Sullivan campaign.

Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, R-Alaska, placed second in the primary last week. Bill Clark / CQ-Roll Call via Getty Images file

The Alaska Supreme Court ruled last month that Dan J. Sullivan can stay on the ballot after the state Division of Elections originally disqualified him. NBC News has reported that state and federal prosecutors in Alaska were investigating whether the race could be part of a conspiracy to confuse voters. A grand jury issued subpoenas this month to compel information from witnesses linked to Dan J. Sullivan’s campaign.

World.title: 5 people and multiple animals killed on rural Oregon property, with suspect found dead
World.content:
A suspect in the killings of five people whose bodies, and those of several animals, were found on a rural property in Oregon was found dead Sunday, officials said.

The Washington County Sheriff’s Office identified Benjamin Charles Parker, 36, as the suspect in the “complex investigation.”

“Officers from the Enumclaw Police Department located Parker’s vehicle and found him deceased inside,” the sheriff’s office said Sunday. “It is believed he died by suicide.”

Enumclaw is a small city in Washington state.

Detectives do not believe the quintuple homicide was random, according to the sheriff’s office. Washington County Sheriff Caprice Massey said they believe Parker “was known to the subjects,” in remarks Sunday night.

Officials initially responded Saturday morning to a 911 call about a vehicle fire in unincorporated Washington County, outside the city of Forest Grove.

Sheriff's and fire personnel found the bodies of five people and “several domestic animals,” officials said. Washington County Sheriff's Office

Washington County Sheriff’s Detective Shannon Wilde said at a news conference Sunday that they are trying to confirm the identities of the victims.

Wilde said the “large scene” is on a rural property with some other homes around and “a lot of vegetation.”

Massey said, “I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex involving this type of an investigation.”

There is no continued threat to the public, according to the sheriff’s office.

Forest Grove is about 25 miles west of Portland, Oregon, and 190 miles southwest of Enumclaw.

World.title: French tourist dies in Death Valley heat after vehicle gets stuck in mud
World.content:
A French tourist died last week in California’s Death Valley after the vehicle he was in got stuck in mud and he ventured away for help in temperatures that reached 116 degrees, officials said.

Pierre Michel Formosa, 68, was with a companion Monday when the vehicle they were using got stuck in mud, the National Park Service said Friday in a news release.

The two set out on foot along the desert salt flats toward the paved Badwater Road, one of the park’s main roadways, to seek help, it said. Formosa said he couldn’t keep going and stopped about 1.3 miles into the trek, according to the park service.

The companion made it to the road and flagged down a driver at about 2 p.m., it said, triggering a search for Formosa that included park rangers and a California Highway Patrol helicopter.

Searchers found Formosa’s body that afternoon, about 1.5 miles from Badwater Road, the park service said.

Death Valley National Park Superintendent Mike Reynolds offered condolences to Formosa’s family. “This is a heartbreaking reminder of how quickly conditions here can turn dangerous,” he said in a statement.

The location of Formosa and his companion’s vehicle is near a hiking trail in a historic mining area, according to the independent archive of the park service.

The National Weather Service issued an extreme heat warning for the area through Sunday night, warning of “dangerously hot conditions.” High temperatures in Death Valley were expected to remain in the 115- to 118-degree range Monday and Tuesday, with a high of 119 expected Wednesday.

The park service urged visitors to stay on paved roads during times of extreme heat, carry satellite phones or beacons and have plenty of drinking water on hand.

“Death Valley is an extraordinary place,” Reynolds said, “but its heat, distances, and remoteness can be dangerous, regardless of experience.”

World.title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
World.content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called steep new U.S. tariffs on a wide swath of his country’s goods “a miscalculation” Saturday morning after trade talks with Canada collapsed late Friday.

Carney blamed the breakdown of talks on what he said were the Trump administration’s “uneconomic” and “unfair” demands.

The 50% tariffs affect about $20 billion worth of U.S. imports from Canada, according to the U.S. Trade Representative’s Office. The import taxes will hit everything from hockey sticks to some building materials, liquors and certain kinds of clothing.

Carney said Canada was pursuing a “focused response,” with tariffs on the U.S. “concentrated in sectors such as steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.” The duties would take effect Sept. 8, he said.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Saturday morning in an interview on Fox News: “We don’t have new talks planned with the Canadians. We’ve said enough, and so we’ve taken countermeasures.” He also said the U.S. would “respond to Canadian retaliation.”

Kyle Kirkwood wins IndyCar race in downtown D.C. celebrating U.S. 250th birthday

The U.S. Capitol behind vehicles on the track during the Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington on Sunday. Elizabeth Frantz / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Blasting down those iconic and bumpy streets with a view of the U.S. Capitol from his car, Florida native Kyle Kirkwood took the checkered flag to win a once-in-a-lifetime IndyCar race on a sunny Sunday.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix was an elaborate 250-mile spectacle in Washington with few expenses spared to celebrate the country’s semiquincentennial, bringing the city a rare blend of power, money and speed.

Kyle Kirkwood celebrates after winning the Freedom 250 Grand Prix on Sunday. Finn Gomez / Getty Images

Kirkwood, who races for Andretti Global, started second but took the lead on the opening lap with a daring maneuver around the outside of pole-sitter and championship leader Alex Palou in front of the National Archives. From there, he proved unbeatable.

Reaching top speeds of about 180 mph, the cars zipped down Pennsylvania Avenue between the Capitol and the White House, the longest straight on the track. They raced past the D.C. courthouse and the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum on the seven-corner track.

“You can’t even put it in words. This is incredible,” Kirkwood said in a postrace interview. “Man, that was a hard race. One hundred forty-seven laps. I’m out of breath right now.”

‘Meet the Press’

Sen. Tim Scott defended Sen. Darline Graham, his fellow South Carolina Republican, ahead of Tuesday’s special GOP primary runoff, dismissing concerns over her national security debate blunder last week.

“Darline Graham is the real deal,” Scott told NBC News’ “Meet the Press,” calling her “highly qualified, incredibly competent, ready for primetime.”

Scott backed Graham just days after she was asked whether Taiwan and the South China Sea are important national security issues. In a viral moment, Graham responded: “I’m just going to be honest here. I’m not, on national security, I’m not that informed on national security, so, but I do support the military.”

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., told “Meet the Press” that he’s “kicking the tires” on a potential 2028 presidential bid.

“We need to be against the status quo, and that’s why I’ve been kicking the tires as I look at 2028, because I don’t think the Democratic Party has answered the call about how we’re going to make sure we have an economy that really does work for everybody, especially working people,” he said.

Politics in Brief

Trailblazer: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, a Kansas governor’s daughter who became the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate without following a spouse into office , has died at 94.

Nancy Kassebaum Baker, a Kansas governor’s daughter who became the , has died at 94. Political beef: GOP lawmakers criticized Trump’s decision to suspend tariffs on ground beef imports over the impact it will have on farmers.

GOP lawmakers to suspend tariffs on ground beef imports over the impact it will have on farmers. Bipartisanship: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., recently met privately with Jared Kushner, and they discussed possible areas of cooperation, a source familiar with the meeting confirmed to NBC News.

Human-caused wildfire forcing thousands to evacuate near Reno, Nevada

The Hawk Fire spreads in Reno, Nev., this month. KRNV

A fast-growing wildfire destroying homes in northwest Reno, Nevada, on Sunday was human-caused and uncontained, authorities said as they encouraged 90,000 people to evacuate. At least six people were injured.

The Hawk Fire began Saturday and quickly grew to 20 square miles as it spread across the Peavine Peak area of Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest, where rugged foothills are ringed by homes and businesses near the California line.

The fire moved exceptionally fast Saturday night, jumping over fire trucks and making it difficult for responders to get to hot spots while residents were trying to get out, Washoe County Sheriff Darin Balaam said.

Several structures were destroyed, and the injured included three civilians and three first responders, officials said. They did not provide additional details about how the fire was started, saying it was under investigation.

Sean Grayson, ex-deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey, dies, attorney says

Sonya Massey talks with Sangamon County Sheriff’s Deputy Sean Grayson outside her home in Springfield, Ill., on July 6, 2024. Illinois State Police via AP file

Sean Grayson, the former Illinois sheriff’s deputy convicted of fatally shooting Sonya Massey in her home in 2024 after she called 911 to report a prowler, has died at 32, his attorney said Sunday.

He was six months into his 20-year sentence for second-degree murder. Grayson was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2023, another defense attorney had said.

It was not immediately clear if cancer is what caused Grayson’s death.

Mark Ruffalo denies antisemitism charge from Paramount Skydance over merger criticism

A Paramount water tower; Mark Ruffalo. Getty Images file

Mark Ruffalo is pushing back against Paramount Skydance after the media giant characterized his anti-merger comments as antisemitic. Ruffalo called the accusation “appalling and fundamentally dishonest.”

The dispute traces to a social media post from the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions movement — a Palestinian-led campaign opposing Israel’s occupation, which began in 1967 — that Ruffalo had boosted.

The post featured comments from Oracle Executive Vice Chair Safra Catz describing the company’s assistance to Israel following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack.

Ruffalo reshared the post to his Instagram Story on Friday, taking aim at Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison — who backed his son David Ellison’s acquisition of Paramount Global through Skydance Media. Ruffalo argued that Larry Ellison is “using [Oracle] to fund his son David’s Warner Bros acquisition.”

Ruffalo urged his followers to push back against the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, arguing it would be “catastrophic for our film industry” through job losses, higher cable costs and reduced competition.

The merger remains on hold, possibly until June, while a federal judge considers a lawsuit from a coalition of state attorneys general challenging the deal over antitrust grounds.

Notable quote

“We have never been afraid. All of their actions — whether blockades or other military moves they have made — have failed, and this new issue of theirs will fail, as well.” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi

Iran’s foreign minister dismissed the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation, saying the measures would fail to defeat Tehran.
